units.zh: 唐檀字子产，豫章南昌人也。
units.en: Tang Tan, styled Zichan, came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.
units.literal: Tang Tan, courtesy name Zichan, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

units.zh: 少游太学，习《京氏易》、《韩诗》、《颜氏春秋》，尤好灾异星占。
units.en: As a young man he attended the Imperial Academy, mastering the Jing Yi, the Han Poetry, and Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals, with a particular passion for omens, prodigies, and astrology.
units.literal: In his youth he studied at the Imperial Academy, learning the Jing family's Changes, the Han Poetry, and the Yan clan's Spring and Autumn Annals, and he was especially fond of portents, anomalies, and stellar divination.

units.zh: 后还乡里，教授常百余人。
units.en: He later went home and taught, often keeping well over a hundred students.
units.literal: Later he returned to his home region and regularly had more than a hundred pupils whom he instructed.

units.zh: 元初七年，郡界有芝草生，太守刘祗欲上言之，以问檀。
units.en: In Yuanchu 7, auspicious fungus appeared inside the commandery. Prefect Liu Zhi wanted to report it to the court and consulted Tang Tan.
units.literal: In the seventh year of the Yuanchu era, lingzhi fungus sprouted within the commandery's borders; Grand Administrator Liu Zhi wished to memorialize the throne about it and asked Tan about it.

units.zh: 檀对曰：“方今外戚豪盛，阳道微弱，斯岂嘉瑞乎？”
units.en: Tan answered, "The imperial in-laws are rampant and the masculine principle is enfeebled—can this really count as an auspicious sign?"
units.literal: Tan replied, saying, "At present the maternal relatives are powerful and overbearing, while the way of yang is weak; how could this be a felicitous omen?"

units.zh: 祗乃止。
units.en: Liu Zhi dropped the idea.
units.literal: Zhi then stopped.

units.zh: 永宁元年，南昌有妇人生四子，祗复问檀变异之应。
units.en: In Yongning 1 a Nanchang woman bore four sons at once. Liu Zhi again pressed Tan on what such a prodigy foretold.
units.literal: In the first year of the Yongning era, a woman in Nanchang gave birth to four sons; Zhi again asked Tan what these anomalies portended.

units.zh: 檀以为京师当有兵气，其祸发于萧墙。
units.en: Tan believed the capital would soon see the shadow of civil strife, with the harm arising inside the court itself.
units.literal: Tan thought that the capital region ought to have an aura of warfare, and that the disaster would break out within the palace walls.

units.zh: 至延光四年，中黄门孙程扬兵殿省，诛皇后兄车骑将军阎显等，立济阴王为天子，果如所占。
units.en: In Yanguang 4 the Yellow Gate eunuch Sun Cheng mobilized forces in the palace, killed the empress's brother, the chariots-and-cavalry general Yan Xian, and his faction, and enthroned the prince of Jiyin—exactly as Tan had predicted.
units.literal: By the fourth year of the Yanguang era, Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gate Sun Cheng had raised troops in the palace offices, executed the empress's elder brother, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yan Xian and others, and set up the Prince of Jiyin as Son of Heaven; it turned out just as he had divined.

units.zh: 永建五年，举孝廉，除郎中。
units.en: Yongjian 5 he was nominated filial and incorrupt and made a gentleman of the palace.
units.literal: In the fifth year of the Yongjian era he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and was appointed gentleman of the palace.

units.zh: 是时白虹贯日，檀因上便宜三事，陈其咎征。
units.en: When a white rainbow spanned the sun, Tan memorialized three practical proposals, spelling out the ominous portents they implied.
units.literal: At that time a white rainbow pierced the sun; Tan therefore submitted three items of timely advice, setting forth the signs of blame.

units.zh: 书奏，弃官去。
units.en: After his memorial went in, he resigned his post and walked away.
units.literal: When the memorial was presented, he abandoned his office and left.

units.zh: 著书二十八篇，名为《唐子》。
units.en: He composed twenty-eight chapters collected under the title Master Tang.
units.literal: He wrote twenty-eight pieces, which he entitled The Master Tang.

units.zh: 卒于家。
units.en: He died at home.
units.literal: He died at home.

units.zh: 公沙穆
units.en: Gongsha Mu
units.literal: Gongsha Mu

units.zh: 公沙穆字文乂，北海胶东人也。
units.en: Gongsha Mu, styled Wenyi, was a native of Jiaodong in Beihai.
units.literal: Gongsha Mu, courtesy name Wenyi, was a man of Jiaodong in Beihai.

units.zh: 家贫贱，自为兒童不好戏弄，长习《韩诗》、《公羊春秋》，尤锐思《河》、《洛》推步之术。
units.en: Though his household was humble, he shunned childish games, and as an adult he trained in the Han Poetry and the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, devoting special energy to the Hetu-Luoshu methods of celestial calculation.
units.literal: His family was poor and of low status; from the time he was a child he did not like frivolous play, and when grown he studied the Han Poetry and the Gongyang Spring and Autumn Annals, and he was especially keen to ponder the numerology of the Yellow River Chart and the Luo River Writing.

units.zh: 居建成山中，依林阻为室，独宿无侣。
units.en: He lived deep in the Jian range, roofed a hut against the woods and cliffs, and slept there utterly alone.
units.literal: He dwelt in the Jian Mountains, relying on forest and rugged terrain to make a chamber, and slept alone without a companion.

units.zh: 时，暴风震雷，有声于外，呼穆者三，穆不与语。
units.en: Once, amid howling wind and thunder, something outside called his name three times; he refused to answer.
units.literal: At one time a violent wind and thunder shook the place, and there was a voice outside calling Mu three times, but Mu would not answer it.

units.zh: 有顷，呼者自牖而入，音状甚怪，穆诵经自若，终亦无它妖异，时人奇之。
units.en: Presently the voice slipped in through the window, weird in timbre and shape, yet Mu went on chanting his texts undisturbed, and nothing further happened—onlookers marveled at his composure.
units.literal: After a while the caller entered through the window, its voice and form very strange; Mu recited his scriptures as calmly as before, and in the end there was no other uncanny incident; people of the time thought him extraordinary.

units.zh: 后遂隐居东莱山，学者自远而至。
units.en: He later withdrew to Mount Donglai, where students journeyed from distant places to study with him.
units.literal: Later he therefore lived in seclusion on Mount Donglai, and scholars came from afar to join him.

units.zh: 有富人王仲，致产千金。
units.en: A wealthy local, Wang Zhong, had amassed a fortune of a thousand catties of gold.
units.literal: There was a rich man, Wang Zhong, whose property amounted to a thousand in gold.

units.zh: 谓穆曰：“方今之世，以货自通，吾奉百万与子为资，何如？”
units.en: Wang said to Mu, "These days connections are bought with money. I will give you a million cash as seed money—will you take it?"
units.literal: He said to Mu, "In the world of today one advances by wealth; I offer you a million in cash as capital—what do you say?"

units.zh: 对曰：“来意厚矣。
units.en: Mu replied, "Your kindness is deep.
units.literal: Mu replied, saying, "Your intention is generous.

units.zh: 夫富贵在天，得之有命。
units.en: Riches and rank rest with Heaven; who receives them is a matter of destiny.
units.literal: Wealth and honor lie with Heaven; obtaining them has to do with fate.

units.zh: 以货求位，吾不忍也。”
units.en: I will not trade cash for an appointment."
units.literal: To seek office with money is something I cannot bear to do."

units.zh: 后举孝廉，以高第为主事，迁缯相。
units.en: He was later nominated filial and incorrupt, placed first in the cohort, made a principal clerk, and promoted to magistrate of Zeng.
units.literal: Later he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt; because of his high ranking he became a director of affairs and was promoted to minister of Zeng.

units.zh: 时缯侯刘敞，东海恭王之后也，所为多不法，废嫡立庶，傲很放恣。
units.en: The marquis of Zeng, Liu Chang, was a descendant of the prince of Donghai; his conduct was often lawless—he deposed his rightful heir in favor of a younger son by a concubine and ruled with swaggering brutality.
units.literal: At that time the marquis of Zeng, Liu Chang, was a descendant of Prince Gong of the East Sea; what he did was often not in accord with the law—he set aside the heir born of the principal wife and established a son by a concubine, and he was arrogant, cruel, and wanton.

units.zh: 穆到官，谒曰：“臣始除之日，京师咸谓臣曰‘缯有恶侯’，以吊小相。
units.en: On taking office Mu presented himself and said, "The day my commission was issued, everyone at court told me, 'Zeng is cursed with a vicious marquis,' and condoled me as if I were walking into a trap.
units.literal: When Mu arrived at his post he paid a formal visit, saying, "On the day I first received my appointment everyone in the capital said to me, 'Zeng has a wicked marquis,' and offered condolences to the petty minister.

units.zh: 明侯何因得此丑声之甚也？
units.en: How, my lord, did you earn a name this foul?
units.literal: How did the enlightened marquis come to have so extremely ugly a reputation?

units.zh: 幸承先人之支体，传茅土之重，不战战兢兢，而违越法度，故朝廷使臣为辅。
units.en: You have inherited your forebears' flesh and blood and the solemn charge of your fief, yet you trample the law instead of walking in fear—so the court dispatched me to stand at your side.
units.literal: You are fortunate to inherit the limbs left you by your ancestors and the weight of the fief and its soil; instead of trembling with caution you transgress the statutes, and therefore the court has sent me as your assistant.

units.zh: 愿改往修来，自求多福。”」
units.en: I urge you to mend your ways and win your own good fortune."
units.literal: I hope you will mend past errors and cultivate the future, and seek blessing for yourself."

units.zh: 乃上没敞所侵官民田地，废其庶子，还立嫡嗣。
units.en: He then reported the lands Chang had seized from officials and commoners for confiscation, annulled the concubine's son as heir, and reinstated the legitimate successor.
units.literal: He then memorialized to confiscate the fields and lands that Chang had seized from officials and commoners, deposed his son by the concubine, and restored the heir of the principal line.

units.zh: 其苍头兒客犯法，皆收考之。
units.en: Every bondservant or client who broke the law was seized and examined.
units.literal: His household retainers and young retainers who broke the law were all arrested and interrogated.

units.zh: 因苦辞谏敞，敞涕泣为谢，多从其所规。
units.en: Mu remonstrated until it hurt; Chang wept and apologized, and largely yielded to his counsel.
units.literal: Because he remonstrated with Chang with bitter earnestness, Chang wept tears of apology and for the most part followed what he urged.

units.zh: 迁弘农令。
units.en: He was promoted to magistrate of Hongnong.
units.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Hongnong.

units.zh: 县界有螟虫食稼，百姓惶惧。
units.en: Crop-eating caterpillars swarmed the county, and the people panicked.
units.literal: Within the county borders caterpillar larvae devoured the crops, and the common people were terrified.

units.zh: 穆乃设坛谢曰：“百姓有过，罪穆之由，请以身祷。”
units.en: Mu built an altar and took the blame: "If the people have sinned, the fault is mine; let me offer myself in prayer."
units.literal: Mu then set up an altar and apologized, saying, "If the common people have fault, the guilt is Mu's doing; I ask to pray with my own body."

units.zh: 于是暴雨，不终日，既霁而螟虫自销，百姓称曰神明，永寿元年，霖雨大水，三辅以东莫不湮没。
units.en: A cloudburst followed, and before nightfall the skies cleared; the pests disappeared on their own, and the locals hailed him as a spirit. In Yongshou 1 ceaseless rains brought floods that drowned everything east of the capital region.
units.literal: Thereupon there was a violent rain, and before the day was over it cleared, after which the caterpillar larvae vanished of themselves; the common people called him divine. In the first year of the Yongshou era there was continuous heavy rain and great flooding, and from the Three Adjuncts eastward nothing was not submerged.

units.zh: 穆明晓占候，乃豫告令百姓徙居高地，故弘农人独得免害。
units.en: Mu read the omens and warned everyone to relocate to high ground, so Hongnong alone was spared.
units.literal: Mu understood prognostication by celestial signs and therefore beforehand instructed the people to move to high ground, and therefore the people of Hongnong alone escaped harm.

units.zh: 迁辽东属国都尉，善得吏人欢心。
units.en: He rose to commandant of the Liaodong dependent state and won the affection of officials and commoners alike.
units.literal: He was promoted to commandant of the dependent state attached to Liaodong and was good at winning the hearts of clerks and people.

units.zh: 年六十六，卒官。
units.en: He died in post at sixty-six.
units.literal: At age sixty-six he died in office.

units.zh: 六子皆知名。
units.en: All six of his sons made a name for themselves.
units.literal: His six sons all became known names.

units.zh: 许曼者，汝南平舆人也。
units.en: Xu Man came from Pingyu in Runan.
units.literal: Xu Man was a man of Pingyu in Runan.

units.zh: 祖父峻，字季山，善卜占之术，多有显验，时人方之前世京房。
units.en: His grandfather Xu Jun, styled Jishan, excelled at yarrow divination and racked up striking hits; contemporaries likened him to the Jing Fang of old.
units.literal: His grandfather Jun, courtesy name Jishan, was skilled in the arts of divination by milfoil and had many conspicuous verifications; people of the time compared him to Jing Fang of an earlier age.

units.zh: 自云少尝笃病，三年不愈，乃谒太山请命，行遇道士张巨君，授以方术。
units.en: He said that in youth he lay gravely ill for three years without recovery, then climbed Mount Tai to plead for his life and met the Daoist Zhang Jujun, who handed down esoteric methods.
units.literal: He himself said that in his youth he once had a severe illness that for three years did not heal, and therefore he went to Mount Tai to beg for his life; on the way he met the Daoist adept Zhang Jujun, who taught him formulas and techniques.

units.zh: 所著《易林》，至今行于世。
units.en: His Forest of Changes is still read today.
units.literal: What he wrote, Forest of Changes, circulates in the world down to the present.

units.zh: 曼少传峻学。
units.en: Man in his youth inherited his grandfather's art.
units.literal: In his youth Man transmitted Jun's learning.

units.zh: 桓帝时，陇西太守冯绲始拜郡，开绶笥，有两赤蛇分南北走。
units.en: When Emperor Huan's Longxi prefect Feng Gun first took office and opened his seal box, two crimson snakes shot out, one south, one north.
units.literal: Under Emperor Huan, when Feng Gun had first received appointment as grand administrator of Longxi, he opened the case for his seal-cord, and two red snakes divided, going south and north.

units.zh: 绲令曼筮之，封成，曼曰：“三岁之后，君当为边将，官有东名，当东北行三千里。
units.en: Gun had Man cast the stalks. When the pattern formed, Man said, "Three years hence you will hold a border command; your title will contain the word 'east,' and you will campaign three thousand li toward the northeast.
units.literal: Gun ordered Man to cast milfoil for it; when the hexagram was complete, Man said, "After three years you will become a general on the frontier, your office will have 'east' in its name, and you ought to march three thousand li toward the northeast.

units.zh: 复五年，更为大将军，南征。”
units.en: Five years later you will hold the post of Grand General once more and lead a southern expedition."
units.literal: After another five years you will again be appointed Grand General and campaign south."

units.zh: 延熹元年，绲出为辽东太守，讨鲜卑，至五年，复拜车骑将军，击武陵蛮贼，皆如占。
units.en: In Yanxi 1 he left for Liaodong to fight the Xianbei; by year five he was named chariots-and-cavalry general and crushed the Wuling Man rebels—each step matched the oracle.
units.literal: In the first year of the Yanxi era Gun went out as grand administrator of Liaodong and attacked the Xianbei; by the fifth year he was again appointed general of chariots and cavalry and struck the Wuling Man bandits—everything was as divined.

units.zh: 其余多此类云。
units.en: His other hits followed the same pattern, it is said.
units.literal: The rest were mostly of this sort, it is said.

units.zh: 赵彦者，琅邪人也。
units.en: Zhao Yan hailed from Langye.
units.literal: Zhao Yan was a man of Langye.

units.zh: 少有术学。
units.en: From boyhood he studied occult techniques.
units.literal: In his youth he had learning in the arts.

units.zh: 延熹三年，琅邪贼劳丙与太山贼叔孙无忌杀都尉。
units.en: Yanxi 3 saw the Langye rebel Lao Bing and the Taishan rebel Shusun Wuji murder a commandant.
units.literal: In the third year of the Yanxi era the Langye bandit Lao Bing and the Taishan bandit Shusun Wuji killed a commandant.

units.zh: 攻没琅邪属县，残害吏民。
units.en: They overran Langye's satellite counties, slaughtering officials and civilians.
units.literal: They attacked and overran Langye's dependent counties, cruelly killing clerks and commoners.

units.zh: 朝廷以南阳宗资为讨寇中郎将，杖钺将兵，督州郡合讨无忌。
units.en: The court named Zong Zi of Nanyang bandit-quelling general-in-chief, gave him the ceremonial axe, and ordered him to coordinate commandery forces against Shusun Wuji.
units.literal: The court appointed Zong Zi of Nanyang bandit-quelling general-in-chief, bearing the battle-axe and leading troops, supervising the commanderies and principalities in a joint campaign against Wuji.

units.zh: 彦为陈“孤虚”之法，以贼屯在莒，莒有五阳之地，宜发五阳郡兵，从孤击虚以讨之。
units.en: Yan taught him the orphan-and-void doctrine: the rebels held Ju, a five-yang place, so Zong should mobilize the five yang commanderies and strike their weak points from the void side.
units.literal: Yan for him explained the method of 'solitary void'; because the bandits were encamped at Ju, and Ju lay in the territory of the five yangs, he advised dispatching troops from the five yang commanderies, striking from solitude into void to attack them.

units.zh: 资具以状上，诏书遣五阳兵到。
units.en: Zong laid out the plan; an edict routed the five yang levies to the front.
units.literal: Zi set forth the whole situation in a memorial, and an edict sent the five yang troops to arrive.

units.zh: 彦推遁甲，教以时进兵，一战破贼，燔烧屯坞，徐、兗二州，一时平夷。
units.en: Yan ran the Dunjia calendar and timed the assault; one engagement broke the rebels, torched their forts, and settled Xu and Yan in a single stroke.
units.literal: Yan pushed the Dunjia cycle and taught them when to advance; in one battle they broke the bandits, burned their stockades, and the provinces of Xu and Yan were pacified at one stroke.

units.zh: 樊志张
units.en: Fan Zhizhang
units.literal: Fan Zhizhang

units.zh: 樊志张者，汉中南郑人也。
units.en: Fan Zhizhang was from Nanzheng in Hanzhong.
units.literal: Fan Zhizhang was a man of Nanzheng in Hanzhong.

units.zh: 博学多通，隐身不仕。
units.en: Erudite and widely read, he hid from the world and never took a post.
units.literal: He was broadly learned and conversant with many subjects, and concealed his person and did not take office.

units.zh: 尝游陇西，时破羌将军段颎出征西羌，请见志张。
units.en: On a journey through Longxi he crossed paths with General Who Smashes the Qiang, Duan Jiong, marching west; Jiong asked to meet him.
units.literal: He once traveled in Longxi; at the time General Who Breaks the Qiang, Duan Jiong, was setting out on a western Qiang campaign and requested to see Zhizhang.

units.zh: 其夕，颎军为羌所围数重，因留军中，三日不得去。
units.en: That night Jiong's camp was ringed by Qiang layers deep; detaining Fan in headquarters, he could not break out for three days.
units.literal: That night Jiong's army was surrounded several deep by the Qiang; because he kept Zhizhang in the camp, for three days he could not get away.

units.zh: 夜谓颎曰：“东南角无复羌，宜乘虚引出，住百里，还师攻之，可以全胜。”
units.en: Fan whispered to Jiong, "The southeast corner is clear—slip through there, rest the army a hundred li out, then wheel back for a full victory."
units.literal: In the night he said to Jiong, "On the southeast corner there are no more Qiang; you should take advantage of the gap to lead out, halt a hundred li away, then turn the army back to attack them, and you can achieve complete victory."

units.zh: 颎从之，果以破贼。
units.en: Jiong did so and routed the enemy.
units.literal: Jiong followed this and indeed thereby broke the bandits.

units.zh: 于是以状表闻。
units.en: He then memorialized the court with a full account.
units.literal: Thereupon he set forth the facts in a memorial to inform the throne.

units.zh: 又说其人既有梓慎、焦、董之识，宜冀圣朝，咨询奇异。
units.en: He added that Fan rivaled Zi Shen, Jiao, and Dong in foresight and deserved a summons to advise the throne on prodigies.
units.literal: He further said that this man had the insight of Zi Shen, Jiao Yanshou, and Dong Jun, and ought to be looked to by the sagely court for consultation on the strange and extraordinary.

units.zh: 于是有诏特征，会病终。
units.en: An edict called for his extraordinary recruitment, but he died of illness before he could answer.
units.literal: Thereupon there was an edict for special summons, but he happened to die of illness before responding.

units.zh: 单飏字武宣，山阳湖陆人也。
units.en: Dan Yang, styled Wuxuan, came from Hulu in Shanyang.
units.literal: Dan Yang, courtesy name Wuxuan, was a man of Hulu in Shanyang.

units.zh: 以孤特清苦自立，善明天官、算术。
units.en: He rose through lonely austerity, skilled at reading the sky and working numbers.
units.literal: By standing alone in solitary hardship he established himself, and was good at clarifying celestial patterns and computation.

units.zh: 举孝廉，稍迁太史令，侍中。
units.en: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he climbed to grand astrologer and palace attendant.
units.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and was gradually promoted to grand astrologer and palace attendant.

units.zh: 出为汉中太守，公事免。
units.en: He served as Hanzhong prefect until routine business cost him the job.
units.literal: He went out as grand administrator of Hanzhong but was dismissed for an affair of public business.

units.zh: 后拜尚书，卒于官。
units.en: He was later appointed secretary of the masters of writing and died in that post.
units.literal: Later he was appointed secretary and died in office.

units.zh: 初，熹平末，黄龙见谯，光禄大夫桥玄问飏：“此何祥也？”
units.en: Near the close of the Xiping reign a yellow dragon showed itself at Qiao; Minister Qiao Xuan asked Yang, "What does this portend?"
units.literal: In the beginning, at the end of the Xiping era, a yellow dragon appeared in Qiao; Minister Qiao Xuan asked Yang, "What sort of auspice is this?"

units.zh: 飏曰：“其国当有王者兴。
units.en: Yang said, "A true king will rise in that domain.
units.literal: Yang replied, "That state will have a kingly man arise.

units.zh: 不及五十年，龙当复见，此其应也。”
units.en: Within fifty years the dragon will appear again—that will be the proof."
units.literal: Before fifty years have passed the dragon ought to appear again, and this will be its verification."

units.zh: 魏郡人殷登密记之。
units.en: Yin Deng of Wei commandery quietly wrote it down.
units.literal: A man of Wei commandery, Yin Deng, secretly recorded it.

units.zh: 至建安二十五年春，黄龙复见谯，其冬，魏受禅。
units.en: In the spring of Jian'an 25 the yellow dragon reappeared at Qiao; that winter Wei accepted the Han abdication.
units.literal: By the spring of the twenty-fifth year of the Jian'an era the yellow dragon appeared again in Qiao; that winter Wei received the abdication.

units.zh: 韩说字叔儒，会稽山阴人也。
units.en: Han Shuo, styled Shuru, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
units.literal: Han Shuo, courtesy name Shuru, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 博通五经，尤善图纬之学。
units.en: He mastered the Five Classics broadly and was especially skilled in chart and apocrypha learning.
units.literal: He broadly mastered the Five Classics and was especially skilled in the learning of diagrams and apocrypha.

units.zh: 举孝廉。
units.en: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt.
units.literal: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt.

units.zh: 与议郎蔡邕友善。
units.en: He was close to the consultant Cai Yong.
units.literal: He was on friendly terms with the consultant Cai Yong.

units.zh: 数陈灾眚，及奏赋、颂、连珠。
units.en: He repeatedly reported disasters and portents, and also submitted fu, hymns, and linked pearls.
units.literal: He repeatedly set forth disasters and portents, and also submitted fu, hymns, and linked pearls.

units.zh: 稍迁侍中。
units.en: He gradually rose to palace attendant.
units.literal: He gradually rose to palace attendant.

units.zh: 光和元年十月，说言于灵帝，云其晦日必食，乞百官严装。
units.en: In Guanghe 1, tenth month, Shuo told Emperor Ling that there would certainly be an eclipse on the last day of the month and asked that the officials dress in full readiness.
units.literal: In the tenth month of Guanghe 1, Shuo told Emperor Ling, saying that on the last day of the month there would certainly be an eclipse, and asked that the hundred officials be strictly dressed.

units.zh: 帝从之，果如所言。
units.en: The emperor followed this, and it happened just as he said.
units.literal: The emperor followed it, and it was indeed as he had said.

units.zh: 中平二年二月，又上封事，克期宫中有灾。
units.en: In Zhongping 2, second month, he again submitted a sealed memorial, fixing a date for a disaster in the palace.
units.literal: In the second month of Zhongping 2, he again submitted a sealed memorial, fixing a date on which there would be a disaster in the palace.

units.zh: 至日南宫大火。
units.en: On that day the Southern Palace caught fire.
units.literal: When the day arrived, the Southern Palace had a great fire.

units.zh: 迁说江夏太守，公事免，年七十，卒于家。
units.en: Shuo was transferred to governor of Jiangxia, was dismissed over official business, and died at home at seventy.
units.literal: Shuo was transferred to be governor of Jiangxia, was dismissed over official business, and died at home at the age of seventy.

units.zh: 董扶字茂安，广汉绵竹人也。
units.en: Dong Fu, styled Mao'an, was a native of Mianzhu in Guanghan.
units.literal: Dong Fu, courtesy name Mao'an, was a man of Mianzhu in Guanghan.

units.zh: 少游太学，与乡人任安齐名，俱事同郡杨厚，学图谶。
units.en: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy alongside his townsman Ren An; both studied charts and apocrypha under Yang Hou of their commandery.
units.literal: In his youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and, with his fellow townsman Ren An, was equally renowned; both served Yang Hou of the same commandery and studied charts and prophecies.

units.zh: 还家讲授，弟子自远而至。
units.en: Back home he taught, and students traveled from afar to hear him.
units.literal: Returning home he lectured, and disciples came from afar.

units.zh: 前後宰府十辟，公車三徵，再舉賢良方正、博士、有道，皆稱疾不就。
units.en: The offices of the chief ministers summoned him ten times, the coach office thrice, and he twice received nominations as worthy, good, incorrupt, erudite, and possessed of the Way—each time he pleaded illness and stayed home.
units.literal: Formerly and later the offices of chief ministers summoned him ten times, the imperial coach three times, and he was twice recommended as worthy and good, incorrupt, erudite, and possessed of the Way; in every case he pleaded illness and did not go.

units.zh: 靈帝時，大將軍何進薦扶，徵拜侍中，甚見器重。
units.en: Emperor Ling's regent He Jin recommended him; summoned as palace attendant, he won deep favor.
units.literal: Under Emperor Ling, Grand General He Jin recommended Fu; he was summoned and appointed palace attendant and was greatly valued.

units.zh: 扶私謂太常劉焉曰：「京師將亂，益州分野有天子氣。」
units.en: Privately he told Minister Liu Yan, "The capital will soon convulse; the Yizhou sky sector carries the qi of an emperor."
units.literal: Fu privately said to Minister Liu Yan, "The capital is about to fall into chaos; in the field division of Yi province there is the aura of a Son of Heaven."

units.zh: 焉信之，遂求出为益州牧，扶亦为蜀郡属国都尉，相与入蜀。
units.en: Yan believed him, begged a posting as Yi provincial shepherd, and entered Shu with Fu, who became commandant of Shu's dependent state.
units.literal: Yan believed it, and therefore sought appointment as shepherd of Yi province; Fu also became commandant of the dependent state attached to Shu commandery, and together they entered Shu.

units.zh: 去後一歲，帝崩，天下大亂，乃去官還家。
units.en: A year after they departed the emperor died and the empire collapsed, so Fu resigned and went home.
units.literal: One year after they left, the emperor died and the realm fell into great chaos, and therefore he left office and returned home.

units.zh: 年八十二卒。
units.en: He died at eighty-two.
units.literal: He died at age eighty-two.

units.zh: 後劉備稱天子於蜀，皆如扶言。
units.en: When Liu Bei later declared himself emperor in Shu, every word of Fu's prophecy had come true.
units.literal: Later Liu Bei declared himself Son of Heaven in Shu; everything was as Fu had said.

units.zh: 蜀丞相诸葛亮问广汉秦密，董扶及任安所长。
units.en: Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang asked the Guanghan scholar Qin Mi what Dong Fu and Ren An respectively excelled at.
units.literal: The Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi of Guanghan what Dong Fu and Ren An were each good at.

units.zh: 密曰：“董扶褒秋毫之善，贬纤介之恶。
units.en: Mi replied, "Dong Fu magnifies goodness no larger than an autumn hair and magnifies fault no smaller than a mote.
units.literal: Mi said, "Dong Fu praises the good as fine as an autumn hair and condemns the evil as small as a fiber.

units.zh: 任安记人之善，忘人之过”云。
units.en: Ren An remembers others' virtues and forgets their slips," or so the story goes.
units.literal: Ren An remembers people's good points and forgets people's faults," it is said.

units.zh: 郭玉者，广汉雒人也。
units.en: Guo Yu came from Luo in Guanghan.
units.literal: Guo Yu was a man of Luo in Guanghan.

units.zh: 初，有老父不知何出，常渔钓于涪水，因号涪翁。
units.en: Long ago a vagrant elder appeared from nowhere, always angling on the Fu River, so folk called him the Fu Fisher.
units.literal: In the beginning there was an old man whose origin no one knew; he constantly fished along the Fu River, and therefore was called the Fu Elder.

units.zh: 乞食人间，见有疾者，时下针石，辄应时而效，乃著《针经》、《诊脉法》传于世。
units.en: He begged meals in the markets, yet whenever he saw the sick he needled and lanced them to instant cure, then set down the Canon of Acupuncture and Methods of Pulse Diagnosis for posterity.
units.literal: Begging his food among men, whenever he saw someone ill he would apply needles and lancing stones from time to time, and they would invariably respond in their season with effect; therefore he wrote Canon of Needling and Pulse Diagnosis Method, which were transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 弟子程高，寻求积年，翁乃授之。
units.en: His pupil Cheng Gao hunted him for years before the old man consented to teach him.
units.literal: His disciple Cheng Gao sought him for accumulated years, and only then did the elder transmit it to him.

units.zh: 高亦隐迹不仕。
units.en: Cheng Gao likewise vanished into reclusion and never served.
units.literal: Gao likewise concealed his traces and did not take office.

units.zh: 玉少师事高，学方诊六微之技，阴阳隐侧之术。
units.en: As a boy Guo Yu apprenticed himself to Cheng Gao, mastering pulse lore, the six pulse subtleties, and the yin-yang arts of hidden diagnosis.
units.literal: In his youth Yu studied under Gao, learning the techniques of pulse diagnosis and the six subtleties, and the arts of yin-yang and hidden lateral signs.

units.zh: 和帝时，为太医丞，多有效应。
units.en: Under Emperor He he rose to assistant director of the imperial medical office, with a long record of cures.
units.literal: Under Emperor He he became assistant director of the imperial physicians, and in many cases there were effective results.

units.zh: 帝奇之，仍试令嬖臣美手腕者与女子杂处帷中，使玉各诊一手，问所疾苦。
units.en: The emperor, intrigued, hid a favorite with fine wrists among women behind a curtain, thrust out two wrists for Yu to read, and asked him to name the complaint.
units.literal: The emperor thought him extraordinary and then tried ordering a favored minister with beautiful wrists to mingle with women inside a curtain, had Yu each diagnose one hand, and asked what ailments they had.

units.zh: 玉曰：“左阳右阴，脉有男女，状若异人。
units.en: Yu said, "The left pulse is male, the right female—the rhythms differ as if two people wore those wrists.
units.literal: Yu said, "Left is yang, right is yin; the pulses have male and female qualities, as though they belonged to different persons.

units.zh: 臣疑其故。”」
units.en: I smell a trick here."
units.literal: Your servant suspects the reason."

units.zh: 帝叹息称善。
units.en: The emperor sighed and called it masterful.
units.literal: The emperor sighed and praised him.

units.zh: 玉仁爱不矜，虽贫贱厮养，必尽其心力，而医疗贵人，时或不愈。
units.en: He was gentle and never condescending: for paupers and bondsmen he gave his whole heart, yet nobles sometimes walked away uncured.
units.literal: Yu was humane and loving and did not put on airs; though someone might be poor, lowly, or a menial, he was sure to exhaust mind and strength for him, yet when treating great men of rank he sometimes did not succeed.

units.zh: 帝乃令贵人羸服变处，一针即差。
units.en: The emperor then had a consort dress as a commoner and sit apart; one needle and she mended.
units.literal: The emperor therefore ordered a great lady to put on shabby clothes and change her station; with one needle she was cured.

units.zh: 召玉诘问其状。
units.en: He called Yu in and pressed him for an explanation.
units.literal: He summoned Yu and closely questioned him about the situation.

units.zh: 对曰：“医之为言意也。
units.en: Yu answered, "The word 'physician' really means 'intention.'
units.literal: Yu replied, saying, "The word for physician means 'mindfulness.'

units.zh: 腠理至微，随气用巧，针石之间，毫芒即乖。
units.en: The textures beneath the skin are minute; skill must ride the patient's breath, and between needle and stone a hair's width of error misses the mark.
units.literal: The interstices of the flesh are extremely subtle; one must apply skill along with the qi; between needle and lancing stone, a hair's breadth of error is deviation.

units.zh: 神存于心手之际，可得解而不可得言也。
units.en: The spirit lives between heart and hand—known in the doing, impossible to lecture.
units.literal: The spirit dwells between mind and hand; it can be grasped in understanding but cannot be put into words.

units.zh: 夫贵者处尊高以临臣，臣怀怖慑以承之。
units.en: A grandee sits aloft while I cower below—that alone warps the cure.
units.literal: Now the nobleman occupies honor and height and looks down on your servant; your servant harbors fear and trembling in attending him.

units.zh: 其为疗也，有四难焉；
units.en: Treating such men involves four obstacles:
units.literal: In giving treatment there are four difficulties:

units.zh: 自用意而不任臣，一难也；
units.en: They insist on their own notions and refuse to trust the doctor—that is the first;
units.literal: He follows his own ideas and will not trust your servant—that is the first difficulty;

units.zh: 将身不谨，二难也；
units.en: they neglect their own regimen—that is the second;
units.literal: he is not careful in regulating his person—that is the second difficulty;

units.zh: 骨节不强，不能使药，三难也；
units.en: their sinews are too weak to bear the drug—that is the third;
units.literal: his bones and joints are not strong enough to take the medicine—that is the third difficulty;

units.zh: 好逸恶劳，四难也。
units.en: they crave comfort and shun exertion—that is the fourth.
units.literal: he loves ease and hates toil—that is the fourth difficulty.

units.zh: 针有分寸，时有破漏，重以恐惧之心，加以裁慎之志，臣意且犹不尽，何有于病哉！
units.en: Needles demand exact depth, timing has its leaks; stack fear and overcaution on top, and even my full attention cannot land—how should the illness yield!
units.literal: The needle has its inches and fractions, the timing has gaps and leaks; add to that a heart full of fear and a mind bent on excessive caution—even your servant's intentions are not fully realized—what hope is there for the disease!

units.zh: 此其所为不愈也。”
units.en: That is why their treatment fails."
units.literal: This is why what he does does not get well."

units.zh: 帝善其对。
units.en: The emperor judged the answer sound.
units.literal: The emperor approved his reply.

units.zh: 年老卒官。
units.en: He died in post at an advanced age.
units.literal: In old age he died in office.

units.zh: 华佗字元化，沛国谯人也，一名旉。
units.en: Hua Tuo, styled Yuanhua, hailed from Qiao in Pei—also known as Hua Fu.
units.literal: Hua Tuo, courtesy name Yuanhua, was a man of Qiao in the Principality of Pei; he had another name, Fu.

units.zh: 游学徐土，兼通数经。
units.en: He wandered the Xu region for study and absorbed more than one classic.
units.literal: He traveled and studied in the land of Xu and was conversant with several classics.

units.zh: 晓养性之术，年且百岁而犹有壮容，时人以为仙。
units.en: He knew the arts of nurturing life: nearing a century he still looked robust, so folk took him for a transcendent.
units.literal: He understood the arts of nurturing life; his years were nearly a hundred yet he still had a vigorous countenance, and people of the time thought him an immortal.

units.zh: 沛相陈珪举孝廉，太尉黄琬辟，皆不就。
units.en: Pei chancellor Chen Gui nominated him filial and incorrupt; Minister Huang Wan called him to office—he declined both.
units.literal: The chancellor of Pei, Chen Gui, recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; Minister of Works Huang Wan summoned him; in neither case did he go.

units.zh: 精于方药，处齐不过数种，心识分铢，不假称量，针灸不过数处。
units.en: He excelled at formulary: a handful of drugs sufficed, each dose weighed in his mind to the fraction of a coin, and his needles never needed many points.
units.literal: He was expert in formulas and drugs; his prescriptions used no more than a few ingredients; he knew weights to the fen and zhu without needing a scale, and his acupuncture used no more than a few points.

units.zh: 若疾发结于内，针药所不能及者，乃令先以酒服麻沸散，既醉无所觉，因刳破腹背，抽割积聚。
units.en: When a malady knotted deep inside, beyond needle or herb, he dosed the patient with hemp-boil powder in wine; once insensible he opened belly or back and cut the growth away.
units.literal: If a disease had formed a knot inside so that needle and drug could not reach it, he would first have them take mafeisan dissolved in wine; once drunk insensible, he would then cut open the abdomen or back and excise the accumulations.

units.zh: 若在肠胃，则断截湔洗，除去疾秽，既而缝合，傅以神膏，四五日创愈，一月之间皆平复。
units.en: Organs in the gut he sectioned, flushed, and cleansed, then sewed the cavity and painted on his miracle paste; within four or five days the wound closed, and in a month the body was whole again.
units.literal: If it was in the stomach or intestines, he would sever, rinse, and wash, removing the diseased filth; then he would sew it closed and apply a numinous salve; in four or five days the wound healed, and within a month all was restored.

units.zh: 佗尝行道，见有病咽塞者，因语之曰：“向来道隅有卖饼人，萍齑甚酸，可取三升饮之，病自当去。”
units.en: Once on the road he met a man choking on something stuck in the throat and told him, "Back at the lane's bend a baker sells sour duckweed brine—drink three pints and it will clear."
units.literal: Tuo once was walking along a road and saw someone ill with blockage of the throat; therefore he said to him, "Just now at the corner of the road there was a man selling cakes; his duckweed pickle is very sour—take three sheng of it to drink and the illness will of itself depart."

units.zh: 即如佗言，立吐一蛇，乃悬于车而候佗。
units.en: The man did so, vomited a live snake, hung it on his cart, and waited for Tuo.
units.literal: The man immediately did as Tuo said, immediately vomited up a snake, then hung it on his cart and waited for Tuo.

units.zh: 时佗小兒戏于门中，逆见，自相谓曰：“客车边有物，必是逢我翁也。”
units.en: Tuo's child was playing at the gate, spied the visitor, and muttered, "Something hangs from that cart—another soul who met Father."
units.literal: At that time Tuo's small child was playing in the doorway, saw him coming from afar, and said to himself, "There is something beside the guest's cart; it must be someone who met my father."

units.zh: 及客进，顾视壁北，悬蛇以十数，乃知其奇。
units.en: When the man stepped inside and glanced at the north wall, a dozen serpents dangled there—then he grasped how uncanny Tuo was.
units.literal: When the guest entered and looked toward the north wall, there were a dozen or more snakes hanging; only then did he realize Tuo's strangeness.

units.zh: 又有一郡守笃病久，佗以为盛怒则差。
units.en: Another prefect lay desperately ill; Tuo judged that only a towering rage would cure him.
units.literal: There was also a grand administrator of a commandery who had been gravely ill a long time; Tuo thought that if he became violently angry he would recover.

units.zh: 乃多受其货而不加功。
units.en: So he pocketed rich fees yet did no work.
units.literal: Therefore he accepted many gifts from him but did not perform the cure.

units.zh: 无何弃去，又留书骂之。
units.en: Soon he walked off, leaving behind a letter that showered abuse on the man.
units.literal: Before long he abandoned him and left, and also left a letter reviling him.

units.zh: 太守果大怒，令人追杀佗，不及，因□恚，吐黑血数升而愈。
units.en: The prefect raged and sent men to murder Tuo, failed to catch him, then spewed several pints of black blood in bilious wrath and recovered.
units.literal: The grand administrator indeed became greatly enraged, ordered men to pursue and kill Tuo, but did not overtake him; because of pent-up fury he vomited several sheng of black blood and recovered.

units.zh: 又有疾者，诣佗求疗，佗曰：“君病根深，应当剖破腹。
units.en: Another patient begged for help; Tuo said, "Your sickness runs too deep—we must open the abdomen.
units.literal: There was also someone ill who went to Tuo seeking treatment; Tuo said, "Sir, the roots of your disease are deep; you ought to have your belly cut open.

units.zh: 然君寿亦不过十年，病不能相杀也。”
units.en: Yet you will not live out ten years; this ailment cannot shorten your span."
units.literal: Yet your lifespan will not exceed ten years in any case; the disease cannot kill you before that."

units.zh: 病者不堪其苦，必欲除之，佗遂下疗，应时愈。
units.en: The man could not bear the pain and demanded surgery; Tuo operated and cured him at once.
units.literal: The sick man could not endure the suffering and insisted on having it removed; Tuo therefore carried out the treatment, and he recovered on the spot.

units.zh: 十年竟死。
units.en: Ten years later he died anyway.
units.literal: After ten years in the end he died.

units.zh: 广陵太守陈登，忽患匈中烦懑，面赤不食。
units.en: Guangling prefect Chen Deng was seized by tightness and burning in the chest, a flushed face, and loss of appetite.
units.literal: Chen Deng, grand administrator of Guangling, suddenly suffered vexation and oppression in his chest, his face was red, and he would not eat.

units.zh: 佗脉之，曰：“府君胃中有虫，欲成内疽，腥物所为也。”
units.en: Tuo felt his pulse and said, "Your stomach harbors worms turning into an inner abscess—blame rank fish."
units.literal: Tuo took his pulse and said, "In your lordship's stomach there are worms about to form an internal abscess; it was caused by rank-smelling food."

units.zh: 即作汤二升，再服，须臾，吐出三升许虫，头赤而动，半身犹是生鱼脍，所苦便愈。
units.en: He brewed two pints of draught; after two doses the man brought up three pints of worms, red-headed and squirming, half still shaped like sashimi—the torment lifted.
units.literal: He immediately prepared two sheng of decoction; after taking it twice, in a little while he vomited upward of three sheng of worms, their heads red and wriggling, half their bodies still raw fish slices; the suffering then departed.

units.zh: 佗曰：“此病后三期当发，遇良医可救。”
units.en: Tuo warned, "It will return three years hence; only a true master can save you then."
units.literal: Tuo said, "This disease will flare again after three cycles; if you meet a skilled physician you can be saved."

units.zh: 登至期疾动，时佗不在，遂死。
units.en: When the day came the sickness returned and Tuo was away, so Chen Deng died.
units.literal: When the appointed time came Deng's illness stirred, but at that time Tuo was not present, and therefore he died.

units.zh: 曹操闻而召佗，常在左右，操积苦头风眩，佗针，随手而差。
units.en: Cao Cao heard of him and kept him close. Plagued by blinding migraines, Cao found instant relief the moment Tuo set needle to skin.
units.literal: Cao Cao heard of him and summoned Tuo; he was constantly at his side. Cao Cao long suffered from splitting headaches with dizziness; Tuo needled him and he was cured as soon as the hand moved.

units.zh: 有李将军者，妻病，呼佗视脉。
units.en: General Li's wife fell ill; Li summoned Tuo to read her pulses.
units.literal: There was a General Li whose wife was ill; he called Tuo to inspect her pulse.

units.zh: 佗曰：“伤身而胎不去。”」
units.en: Tuo said, "The womb is hurt but the child remains inside."
units.literal: Tuo said, "Injury to the body yet the fetus has not departed."

units.zh: 将军言间实伤身，胎已去矣。
units.en: Li protested that she had miscarried—the fetus was gone.
units.literal: The general said that in the interval he had indeed injured her body, but the fetus had already departed.

units.zh: 佗曰：“案脉，胎未去也。”
units.en: Tuo answered, "The pulse says the baby is still there."
units.literal: Tuo said, "According to the pulse, the fetus has not departed."

units.zh: 将军以为不然。
units.en: Li refused to believe him.
units.literal: The general thought this was not so.

units.zh: 妻稍差，百余日复动，更呼佗。
units.en: She rallied for a hundred days, then the pain returned; they called Tuo back.
units.literal: The wife improved somewhat; after more than a hundred days it stirred again, and they again summoned Tuo.

units.zh: 佗曰：“脉理如前，是两胎。
units.en: Tuo said, "The pulses match the earlier reading—you carried twins.
units.literal: Tuo said, "The pulse pattern is as before; this is two fetuses.

units.zh: 先生者去血多，故后兒不得出也。
units.en: The first child bled away so heavily that the second could not follow.
units.literal: The firstborn departed with much loss of blood, and therefore the later child could not come out.

units.zh: 胎既已死，血脉不复归，必燥著母脊。”
units.en: That second fetus is dead; its blood no longer flows, so it has dried fast to your wife's backbone."
units.literal: The fetus having already died, the blood channels no longer return to it; it is sure to dry and adhere to the mother's spine."

units.zh: 乃为下针，并令进汤。
units.en: He needled her lower belly and gave a draught.
units.literal: He therefore applied needles below and also ordered her to drink a decoction.

units.zh: 妇因欲产而不通。
units.en: She labored yet nothing emerged.
units.literal: The woman thereupon wished to give birth but could not pass it.

units.zh: 佗曰：“死胎枯燥，势不自生。”
units.en: Tuo said, "The corpse is mummified; it cannot birth itself."
units.literal: Tuo said, "The dead fetus is desiccated; by its nature it cannot be born alive."

units.zh: 使人探之，果得死胎，人形可识，但其色已黑。
units.en: He had someone probe for it, and out came a black, recognizable stillbirth.
units.literal: He had someone probe for it and indeed obtained a dead fetus; the human form could be recognized, but its color was already black.

units.zh: 佗之绝技，皆此类也。
units.en: Tuo's marvels ran in this vein.
units.literal: Tuo's supreme skills were all of this sort.

units.zh: 为人性恶，难得意，且耻以医见业，又去家思归，乃就操求还取方，因托妻疾，数期不反。
units.en: Proud and restless, he scorned life as a mere doctor, longed for home, begged Cao for leave to fetch recipes, pleaded his wife's sickness, and overstayed every promised return.
units.literal: In personality he was difficult and hard to please, and he was ashamed to make a career of being seen as a physician; moreover he missed home and wished to return, and therefore went to Cao Cao seeking permission to return and fetch formulas, using his wife's illness as a pretext, and repeatedly missed the deadline for coming back.

units.zh: 操累书呼之，又敕郡县发遣，佗恃能厌事，独不肯至。
units.en: Cao wrote again and again and ordered local officials to escort him; Tuo, confident in his gift, sneered at bureaucratic errands and stayed away.
units.literal: Cao Cao repeatedly wrote summoning him and also ordered commanderies and counties to dispatch him, but Tuo, relying on his ability, disdained such service and alone refused to come.

units.zh: 操大怒，使人廉之，知妻诈疾，乃收付狱讯，考验首服。
units.en: Cao boiled over, sent agents, learned the wife sham sick, jailed Tuo, and tortured a confession.
units.literal: Cao Cao was greatly enraged, had men investigate him, learned that his wife feigned illness, then arrested him, handed him to the jailors for interrogation, and under examination he confessed from the first.

units.zh: 荀彧请曰：“佗方术实工，人命所悬，宜加全宥。”
units.en: Xun Yu pleaded, "Tuo's art is superb—lives ride on him—spare him."
units.literal: Xun Yu requested, saying, "Tuo's formulas and techniques are truly masterful; human lives hang on them; he ought to be granted full pardon."

units.zh: 操不从，竟杀之。
units.en: Cao refused and executed him.
units.literal: Cao Cao did not follow this and in the end killed him.

units.zh: 佗临死，出一卷书与狱吏，曰：“此可以活人。”
units.en: At the block he handed the warden a scroll: "This will save lives."
units.literal: When Tuo was about to die he produced one scroll of writing and gave it to the jailor, saying, "This can keep people alive."

units.zh: 吏畏法不敢受，佗不强与，索火烧之。
units.en: The man feared the statute and declined; Tuo did not insist—he burned the book.
units.literal: The clerk feared the law and did not dare accept it; Tuo did not force him but sought fire and burned it.

units.zh: 初，军吏李成苦咳，昼夜不寐。
units.en: A camp clerk named Li Cheng coughed himself sleepless.
units.literal: In the beginning a military clerk, Li Cheng, suffered bitter coughing and could not sleep day or night.

units.zh: 佗以为肠痈，与散两钱服之，即吐二升脓血，于此渐愈。
units.en: Tuo diagnosed gut abscess, gave two measures of powder, and Li vomited two pints of pus and blood before mending.
units.literal: Tuo thought it intestinal abscess and gave him two cash-measures of powder to take; he immediately vomited two sheng of pus and blood and from this gradually recovered.

units.zh: 乃戒之曰：“后十八岁，疾当发动，若不得此药，不可差也。”
units.en: Tuo warned, "In eighteen years it will return; without this same drug you die."
units.literal: Tuo then warned him, saying, "After eighteen years the illness ought to flare; if you cannot obtain this drug, you cannot be cured."

units.zh: 复分散与之，后五六岁，有里人如成先病，请药甚急，成愍而与之，乃故往谯更从佗求，适值见收，意不忍言。
units.en: He split the leftover powder for Li. Five or six years later a neighbor with the same cough begged desperately; Li, moved, gave up his store, then rode to Qiao for more—only to find Tuo in chains, too ashamed to ask.
units.literal: He again divided the powder and gave it to him; after five or six years there was a fellow villager like Cheng who had fallen ill first and urgently begged for the drug; Cheng, pitying him, gave it to him, then purposely went to Qiao to again seek from Tuo, but it happened that Tuo was under arrest, and in his heart he could not bear to speak.

units.zh: 后十八年，成病发，无药而死。
units.en: Eighteen years on the cough returned; Li had no medicine and perished.
units.literal: After eighteen years Cheng's illness broke out; without the drug he died.

units.zh: 广陵吴普、彭城樊阿，皆从佗学。
units.en: Guangling's Wu Pu and Pengcheng's Fan A both trained under Tuo.
units.literal: Wu Pu of Guangling and Fan A of Pengcheng both studied under Tuo.

units.zh: 普依准佗疗，多所全济。
units.en: Wu Pu copied his master's methods and kept countless patients alive.
units.literal: Pu modeled himself on Tuo's treatments and in many cases wholly saved and helped them.

units.zh: 佗语普曰：“人体欲得劳动，但不当使极耳。
units.en: Tuo told him, "The body wants motion—just never to exhaustion.
units.literal: Tuo said to Pu, "The human body desires to get movement, only one ought not to carry it to the extreme.

units.zh: 动摇则谷气得销，血脉流通，病不得生，譬犹户枢，终不朽也。
units.en: Stir the frame and grain qi digests, blood courses, sickness finds no foothold—like a hinge that never rusts.
units.literal: If it is shaken, then the grain qi is consumed, blood channels flow through, and disease cannot arise—like a door pivot, which in the end does not rot.

units.zh: 是以古之仙者，为导引之事，熊经鸱顾，引挽腰体，动诸关节，以求难老。
units.en: Ancient transcendents therefore practiced guided stretching—bear hangs, owl twists—flexing every joint to stall old age.
units.literal: Therefore the immortals of antiquity performed daoyin exercises, bear-stretching and owl-turning, pulling and stretching the waist and body, moving all the joints, in order to seek difficulty in aging.

units.zh: 吾有一术，名五禽之戏：一曰虎，二曰鹿，三曰熊，四曰猿，五曰鸟。
units.en: He taught the Five-Animal Frolic: tiger, deer, bear, ape, and bird.
units.literal: I have one technique, called the Play of the Five Beasts: the first is tiger, the second deer, the third bear, the fourth ape, the fifth bird.

units.zh: 亦以除疾，兼利蹄足，以当导引。
units.en: It drives out disease, limbers the legs, and replaces formal daoyin.
units.literal: It is also used to eliminate illness and at the same time benefits the feet and hooves, serving in place of daoyin.

units.zh: 体有不快，起作一禽之戏，恰而汗出，因以著粉，身体轻便而欲食。”
units.en: Whenever you feel off, perform one animal until you lightly sweat, dust yourself, and hunger returns with a light step."
units.literal: If the body is not at ease, rise and perform the play of one beast, perspire slightly, then apply powder; the body becomes light and agile and desires food."

units.zh: 普施行之，年九十余，耳目聪明，齿牙完坚。
units.en: Wu Pu followed the regimen past ninety with sharp senses and firm teeth.
units.literal: Pu practiced it; at over ninety years of age his ears and eyes were keen and his teeth were intact and firm.

units.zh: 阿善针术。
units.en: Fan A excelled at acupuncture.
units.literal: Fan A was good at the art of needling.

units.zh: 凡医咸言背及匈藏之间不可妄针，针之不可过四分，而阿针背入一二寸，巨阙匈藏乃五六寸，而病皆瘳。
units.en: Doctors warned that needling between spine and vitals must stay shallow—never past four fen—yet Fan drove needles a cun or two into the back and five or six cun into the great-que chest point, curing every case.
units.literal: Generally physicians all say that between the back and the chest and the hidden organs one must not rashly needle, and that needling must not go more than four fen, yet when Fan A needled the back he entered one or two cun, and at the great que point in the chest and hidden organs five or six cun, yet the diseases were all cured.

units.zh: 阿从佗求方可服食益于人者，佗授以漆叶青黏散：漆叶屑一斗，青黏十四两，以是为率。
units.en: Fan A begged for a tonic formula; Tuo passed down lacquer-leaf and green-mugwort powder—one peck of powdered lacquer leaves to fourteen ounces of green mugwort as the ratio.
units.literal: Fan A sought from Tuo a formula that could be ingested and benefit people; Tuo gave him the lacquer-leaf and green-sticky powder: one dou of lacquer-leaf shavings and fourteen liang of green-sticky, using this as the standard proportion.

units.zh: 言久服，去三虫，利五藏，轻体，使人头不白。
units.en: Long use, he claimed, purges the three worms, tones the five viscera, lightens the body, and keeps hair dark.
units.literal: He said that taken long it removes the three worms, benefits the five viscera, lightens the body, and keeps a person's hair from turning white.

units.zh: 阿從其言，壽百餘歲。
units.en: Fan A took it and passed a century in age.
units.literal: Fan A followed his words and lived beyond a hundred years.

units.zh: 漆叶处所而有。
units.en: Lacquer trees grow almost everywhere.
units.literal: Lacquer leaves are found wherever one goes.

units.zh: 青黏生于丰、沛、彭城及朝歌间。
units.en: Green mugwort flourishes between Feng, Pei, Pengcheng, and Zhaoge.
units.literal: Green-sticky grows between Feng, Pei, Pengcheng, and Zhaoge.

units.zh: 汉世异术之士甚众，虽云不经，而亦有不可诬，故简基美者列于传末：
units.en: Han China swarmed with wonder-workers; though many tales skirt orthodoxy, some cannot be dismissed, so I close with the soundest marvels:
units.literal: In the Han age men of strange arts were very numerous; although it is said they were not canonical, there are also things that cannot be slandered; therefore I have selected those with a fine basis and placed them at the end of the biographies:

units.zh: 泠寿光、唐虞、鲁女生三人者，皆与华佗同时。
units.en: Leng Shouguang, Tang Yu, and Lu Nüsheng moved in Hua Tuo's generation.
units.literal: Leng Shouguang, Tang Yu, and Lu Nüsheng—these three persons were all contemporaries of Hua Tuo.

units.zh: 寿光年可百五六十岁，行容成公御妇人法，常屈颈鷮息，须发尽白，而色理如三四十时，死于江陵。
units.en: Shouguang lived perhaps a hundred and sixty years, practiced Rongcheng's sexual yoga, and hissed through a crane neck until hair went white while his face stayed thirty; he died at Jiangling.
units.literal: Shouguang's years may have been one hundred fifty or sixty; he practiced Lord Rongcheng's method of controlling women in intercourse, constantly bent his neck and breathed like a stork; his whiskers and hair were entirely white, yet the color and texture of his complexion were like those of thirty or forty; he died at Jiangling.

units.zh: 唐虞道赤眉、张步家居里落，若与相及，死于乡里不其县。
units.en: Tang Yu walked among Red Eyebrows and Zhang Bu as if neighbor to neighbor, and died in Buqi county.
units.literal: Tang Yu's way was with the Red Eyebrows and Zhang Bu at home in hamlets and villages, as if he had contact with them; he died in his home village in Buqi county.

units.zh: 鲁女生数说显宗时事，甚明了，议者疑其时人也。
units.en: Lu Nüsheng recounted Emperor Ming's reign with eerie clarity, leading some to think he had lived then.
units.literal: Lu Nüsheng several times narrated events of the Manifest Ancestor's time, very clearly; debaters suspected he was a man of that period.

units.zh: 董卓乱后，莫知所在。
units.en: After Dong Zhuo's coup he vanished without trace.
units.literal: After Dong Zhuo's rebellion no one knew where he went.

units.zh: 徐登者，闽中人也。
units.en: Xu Deng came from the Min interior.
units.literal: Xu Deng was a man of Minzhong.

units.zh: 本女子，化为丈夫。
units.en: She had been born a woman but turned into a man.
units.literal: Originally a woman, she transformed into a husband.

units.zh: 善为巫术。
units.en: She excelled at shaman craft.
units.literal: She was good at performing shaman arts.

units.zh: 又赵炳，字公阿，东阳人，能为越方。
units.en: Zhao Bing, styled Gong'a, of Dongyang, wielded southern exorcist rites.
units.literal: There was also Zhao Bing, courtesy name Gong'a, a man of Dongyang, who could perform Yue formulas.

units.zh: 时遭兵乱，疾疫大起，二人遇于乌伤溪水之上，遂结言约，共以其术疗病。
units.en: Amid war and epidemic they met on the Wushang brook, swore an oath, and pooled their arts to heal the sick.
units.literal: At that time, encountering military turmoil, pestilence broke out greatly; the two men met on the waters of the Wushang stream and therefore made a pact in words, jointly using their arts to treat illness.

units.zh: 各相谓曰：“今既同志，且可各试所能。”
units.en: They said to each other, "We are of one mind—let each prove his art."
units.literal: Each said to the other, "Now that we share the same purpose, we may each try our abilities."

units.zh: 登乃禁溪水，水为不流；
units.en: Xu Deng stopped the brook midstream until the current froze;
units.literal: Deng then sealed off the stream water, and the water ceased to flow;

units.zh: 炳复次禁枯树，树即生荑，二人相视而笑，共行其道焉。
units.en: Zhao Bing then charmed a dead tree until it leafed out; they exchanged a smile and went on demonstrating their craft.
units.literal: Bing next again sealed a withered tree, and the tree immediately sprouted shoots; the two looked at each other and laughed, and together practiced their way.

units.zh: 登年长，炳师事之。
units.en: Xu Deng was the senior, so Zhao Bing treated him as master.
units.literal: Deng was the elder in years, and Bing served him as teacher.

units.zh: 贵尚清俭，礼神唯以东流水为酌，削桑皮为脯。
units.en: Zhao Bing, having apprenticed himself to the austere Deng, poured only east-running water for the gods and shaved mulberry bark into jerky for offerings.
units.literal: Bing valued purity and frugality; in worshipping the spirits he used only east-flowing water for libations and shaved mulberry bark for dried meat.

units.zh: 但行禁架，所疗皆除。
units.en: Their sealing spells lifted every ailment they touched.
units.literal: Whenever they performed sealing and binding, what they treated was all removed.

units.zh: 后登物故，炳东入章安，百姓未之知也。
units.en: After Xu Deng died, Zhao Bing moved east to Zhang'an, still unknown to the locals.
units.literal: Later Deng passed away; Bing went east into Zhang'an, and the common people did not yet know of him.

units.zh: 炳乃故升茅屋，梧鼎而爨，主人见之惊□，炳笑不应。
units.en: Zhao Bing climbed a thatched roof, braced a cauldron, and lit a cookfire; the innkeeper stared speechless while Zhao laughed and said nothing.
units.literal: Bing therefore purposely climbed onto a thatched hut, set up a tripod, and cooked; when the host saw it he was startled and speechless; Bing laughed and did not answer.

units.zh: 既而□孰，屋无损异。
units.en: Soon the meal was ready, yet the thatch never scorched.
units.literal: Before long the food was done, and the house had no damage or anomaly.

units.zh: 又尝临水求度，船人不和之，炳乃张盖坐其中，长啸呼风，乱流而济，于是百姓神服，从者如归。
units.en: Once he needed a ferry and the boatman refused; Zhao spread his umbrella, sat beneath it, whistled up a wind, and shot across the chop—onlookers hailed him as a god, and disciples flocked like kin coming home.
units.literal: He also once sought to cross by the water's edge; the boatman would not harmonize with him, whereupon Bing spread his canopy and sat inside it, gave a long whistle and called the wind, crossed the turbulent current, and therefore the common people thought him divine and submitted; followers were like returning home.

units.zh: 章安令恶其惑众，收杀之。
units.en: The Zhang'an magistrate, hating his sway over the crowd, had him seized and executed.
units.literal: The magistrate of Zhang'an hated him for deluding the masses and arrested and killed him.

units.zh: 人为立祠室于永康，至今蚊蚋不能入也。
units.en: The people built him a shrine at Yongkang where, even today, no mosquito may enter.
units.literal: People therefore erected a shrine chamber for him in Yongkang; down to the present mosquitoes and gnats cannot enter it.

units.zh: 费长房
units.en: Fei Zhangfang
units.literal: Fei Zhangfang

units.zh: 费长房者，汝南人也。
units.en: Fei Zhangfang came from Runan.
units.literal: Fei Zhangfang was a man of Runan.

units.zh: 曾为市掾。
units.en: He had served as a market clerk.
units.literal: He once was a clerk in the market.

units.zh: 市中有老翁卖药，悬一壶于肆头，及市罢，辄跳入壶中。
units.en: An old apothecary hung a gourd above his stall and, when the market emptied, leapt inside it.
units.literal: In the market there was an old man selling medicine; he hung a gourd at the head of his shop, and when the market closed he always jumped into the gourd.

units.zh: 市人莫之见，唯长房于楼上睹之，异焉，因往再拜奉酒脯。
units.en: Shoppers noticed nothing, but Zhangfang, watching from a balcony, saw the trick, descended, and twice bowed with wine and meat.
units.literal: The people of the market did not see him; only Zhangfang, from an upper story, watched him, thought it strange, and therefore went and twice bowed, presenting wine and dried meat.

units.zh: 翁知长房之意其神也，谓之曰：“子明日可更来。”
units.en: The elder saw his intent and said, "Return tomorrow."
units.literal: The old man knew that Zhangfang's mind considered him divine and said to him, "Tomorrow you may come again."

units.zh: 长房旦日复诣翁，翁乃与俱入壶中。
units.en: At dawn Zhangfang returned, and the sage walked him into the gourd.
units.literal: The next day at dawn Zhangfang again went to visit the old man, and the old man then together with him entered the gourd.

units.zh: 唯见玉堂严丽，旨酒甘肴，盈衍其中，共饮毕而出。
units.en: Inside stood a palace of jade, tables groaning with wine and dainties; they feasted, then stepped back into the world.
units.literal: He only saw a jade hall, stern and splendid, with fine wine and sweet delicacies overflowing within; they drank together to the end and came out.

units.zh: 翁约不听与人言之。
units.en: The old man forbade him to speak of it.
units.literal: The old man enjoined him not to listen to telling people about it.

units.zh: 后乃就楼上候长房曰：“我神仙之人，以过见责，今事毕当去，子宁能相随乎？
units.en: Later the immortal met him upstairs and said, "I belong to the transcendents, banished for a fault; my term is up and I must go—will you follow?
units.literal: Later he then went to the upper story to await Zhangfang and said, "I am a man among the immortals; because of faults I was punished; now my business is finished and I ought to leave—can you, sir, follow along?

units.zh: 楼下有少酒，与卿与别。”
units.en: There is a little wine downstairs for our farewell."
units.literal: Below there is a little wine, to take leave with you."

units.zh: 长房使人取之，不能胜，又令十人扛之，犹不举。
units.en: Zhangfang sent servants to lift the keg; they could not budge it, nor could ten men with poles.
units.literal: Zhangfang sent men to fetch it, but they could not lift it; he again ordered ten men to carry it on poles, and still they could not raise it.

units.zh: 翁闻，笑而下楼，以一指提之而上。
units.en: The sage laughed, strolled down, and carried it up on one finger.
units.literal: When the old man heard, he laughed and came downstairs, lifted it with one finger, and brought it up.

units.zh: 视器如一升许，而二人饮之终日不尽。
units.en: The jar looked to hold a single pint, yet the two drank all day without emptying it.
units.literal: The vessel looked to be about a sheng, yet the two of them drank from it all day without exhausting it.

units.zh: 长房遂欲求道，而顾家人为忧。
units.en: Zhangfang yearned for the Way yet feared for his kin.
units.literal: Zhangfang thereupon wished to seek the Way, but he looked on his family as a worry.

units.zh: 翁乃断一青竹，度与长房身齐，使悬之舍后。
units.en: The sage cut a green bamboo to Zhangfang's height and hung it behind the house.
units.literal: The old man therefore cut a green bamboo staff, measured it even with Zhangfang's body, and had him hang it behind the house.

units.zh: 家人见之，即长房形也，以为缢死，大小惊号，遂殡葬之。
units.en: His household mistook the staff for his corpse—believing he had hanged himself they wailed and buried it.
units.literal: When the family members saw it, it was immediately Zhangfang's form; they thought he had hanged himself; great and small cried out in alarm, and therefore they buried him.

units.zh: 长房立其傍，而莫之见也。
units.en: Zhangfang stood nearby, invisible to all.
units.literal: Zhangfang stood beside them, yet none saw him.

units.zh: 于是遂随从入深山，践荆棘于群虎之中，留使独处，长房不恐。
units.en: He followed into tiger-haunted mountains, was left alone among the brutes, and felt no fear.
units.literal: Thereupon he followed him into the deep mountains, trampled brambles amid a pack of tigers, was left to dwell alone, and Zhangfang was not afraid.

units.zh: 又卧于空室，以朽索悬万斤石于心上，众蛇竞来啮索且断，长房亦不移。
units.en: They laid him in an empty room with a rotting cord holding a ten-thousand-jin rock over his heart; serpents gnawed the strand nearly through, yet he never stirred.
units.literal: He was also made to lie in an empty chamber, with a rotten rope suspending a stone of ten thousand jin above his heart; many snakes came competing to gnaw the rope as it was about to break, yet Zhangfang also did not move.

units.zh: 翁还，抚之曰：“子可教也。”
units.en: When the master returned he stroked him and said, "You may be taught."
units.literal: When the old man returned, he stroked him and said, "You can be taught."

units.zh: 复使食粪，粪中有三虫，臭秽特甚，长房意恶之。
units.en: Next they fed him ordure crawling with three worms; Zhangfang gagged at the stench.
units.literal: He again made him eat dung; inside the dung were three worms, extremely foul and filthy, and Zhangfang's mind reviled it.

units.zh: 翁曰：“子几得道，恨于此不成，如何！”
units.en: The sage sighed, "You nearly attained the Way—this disgust alone undid you!"
units.literal: The old man said, "You were within a little of obtaining the Way; the regret is that here it did not succeed—what can be done!"

units.zh: 长房辞归，翁与一竹杖，曰：“骑此任所之，则自至矣。
units.en: Zhangfang took leave to return; the old man gave him a bamboo staff, saying, "Ride this wherever you wish to go, and you will arrive of yourself.
units.literal: Zhangfang took leave to return; the old man gave him one bamboo staff, saying, "Ride this wherever you wish to go, and you will arrive of yourself.

units.zh: 既至，可以杖投葛陂中也。”
units.en: When you land, throw the staff into Ge Marsh."
units.literal: Once you have arrived, you may cast the staff into Ge Marsh."

units.zh: 又为作一符，曰：“以此主地上鬼神。”
units.en: He added a charm: "This commands every ghost below heaven."
units.literal: He also for him made one talisman, saying, "With this you shall command the ghosts and spirits of the earth."

units.zh: 長房乘杖，須臾來歸，自謂去家適經旬日，而已十餘年矣。
units.en: Zhangfang rode the staff and returned in an instant, thinking he had been gone barely ten days, but more than ten years had passed.
units.literal: Zhangfang rode the staff; in a moment he came home, saying himself that he had been away from home only ten days, yet more than ten years had already passed.

units.zh: 即以杖投陂，顾视则龙也。
units.en: He hurled the staff into the pool and saw a dragon coil away.
units.literal: He immediately cast the staff into the marsh; when he looked back it was a dragon.

units.zh: 家人谓其久死，不信之。
units.en: His kin had mourned him for dead and refused to credit his return.
units.literal: The family members thought he had long been dead and did not believe him.

units.zh: 长房曰：“往日所葬，但竹杖耳。”
units.en: Zhangfang said, "You buried only bamboo."
units.literal: Zhangfang said, "What was buried in former days was only a bamboo staff."

units.zh: 乃发冢剖棺，杖犹存焉。
units.en: They opened the grave and found the staff intact.
units.literal: They therefore opened the tomb and split the coffin; the staff was still there.

units.zh: 遂能医疗众病，鞭笞百鬼，及驱使社公。
units.en: Henceforth he healed every sickness, lashed legions of ghosts, and commanded the village earth-god.
units.literal: Thereupon he was able to heal the multitude of diseases, flog the hundred ghosts, and also drive the earth god of the soil altar.

units.zh: 或在它坐，独自恚怒，人问其故，曰：“吾责鬼魅之犯法者耳。”
units.en: Sometimes he sat alone, visibly furious; asked why, he said, "I am disciplining lawbreaking sprites."
units.literal: Sometimes when he was seated elsewhere, he alone became angry; when people asked the reason, he said, "I am reproaching ghosts and sprites who have violated the law."

units.zh: 汝南岁岁常有魅，伪作太守章服、诣府门椎鼓者，郡中患之。
units.en: Each year Runan suffered a demon who donned the prefect's robes, rode to the yamen gate, and beat the drum—the whole commandery dreaded it.
units.literal: In Runan year after year there was always a goblin that counterfeited the grand administrator's seals and robes, went to the gate of the administration, and beat the drum; the commandery was troubled by it.

units.zh: 时魅适来，而逢长房谒府君，惶惧不得退，便前解衣冠，叩头乞活。
units.en: One day the creature arrived just as Zhangfang called on the prefect; trapped, it stripped its costume and begged for mercy.
units.literal: At that time the goblin happened to come and ran into Zhangfang paying a visit to the lord; in panic and fear it could not retreat, and therefore went forward, removed cap and robes, and knocked its head begging for life.

units.zh: 长房呵之云：“便于中庭正汝故形！”」
units.en: Zhangfang barked, "Show your true shape in the courtyard!"
units.literal: Zhangfang shouted at it, saying, "In the middle courtyard restore your true form!"

units.zh: 即成老鳖，大如车轮，颈长一丈。
units.en: It turned into a giant softshell turtle, wheel-wide, with a neck ten feet long.
units.literal: It immediately became an old soft-shelled turtle, large as a cart wheel, with a neck one zhang long.

units.zh: 长房复令就太守服罪，付其一札，以敕葛陂君。
units.en: He sent the creature to confess its guilt to the prefect and gave it a writ addressed to the spirit lord of Ge Marsh.
units.literal: Zhangfang again ordered it to go to the grand administrator to confess guilt, gave it one slip of writing, and thereby charged the lord of Ge Marsh.

units.zh: 魅叩头流涕，持札植于陂边，以颈绕之而死。
units.en: The demon wept, planted the slip by the marsh, wound its neck about the post, and strangled itself.
units.literal: The goblin knocked its head, weeping tears, held the slip and planted it at the edge of the marsh, wrapped its neck around it, and died.

units.zh: 后东海君来见葛陂君，因淫其夫人，于是长房劾系之三年，而东海大旱。
units.en: Later the Eastern Sea god visited Ge Marsh and seduced its goddess; Zhangfang jailed him three years, and the Eastern Sea withered in drought.
units.literal: Later the lord of the Eastern Sea came to visit the lord of Ge Marsh and thereupon debauched his wife; therefore Zhangfang impeached and bound him for three years, and thereupon the Eastern Sea suffered great drought.

units.zh: 长房至海上，见其人请雨，乃谓之曰：“东海君有罪，吾前系于葛陂，今方出之，使作雨也。”
units.en: Zhangfang walked the shore where priests begged rain and said, "The Eastern Sea deity sinned; I chained him at Ge Marsh and have only now freed him to pour storms."
units.literal: Zhangfang went to the sea and saw the man praying for rain, and therefore said to him, "The lord of the Eastern Sea is guilty; I formerly bound him at Ge Marsh; now I have just released him, to make him produce rain."

units.zh: 于是雨立注。
units.en: Rain fell at once.
units.literal: Thereupon rain poured straight down.

units.zh: 长房曾与人共行，见一书生黄巾被裘，无鞍骑马，下而叩头，长房曰：“还它马，赦汝死罪。”
units.en: Walking with a friend he saw a scholar in yellow headcloth and fur cloak riding bareback; the man kowtowed. Zhangfang said, "Give back the horse and I spare your life."
units.literal: Zhangfang once walked with someone and saw a student in a yellow scarf wearing a fur robe, riding a horse without saddle; he dismounted and knocked his head; Zhangfang said, "Return his horse; I pardon your capital crime."

units.zh: 人问其故，长房曰：“此狸也，盗社公马耳。”
units.en: Asked to explain, he said, "A fox-thief borrowed the village god's mount."
units.literal: People asked him the reason, and Zhangfang said, "This is a fox; it stole the earth god's horse, that is all."

units.zh: 又尝坐客，而使至宛市鲊，须臾还，乃饭。
units.en: Once he feasted guests and sent a runner to Wan for pickled fish; the runner returned in moments and they dined.
units.literal: He also once seated guests and sent someone to Wan market for salted fish; in a moment he returned, and then they ate.

units.zh: 或一日之间，人见其在千里之外者数处焉。
units.en: In a single day folk spotted him a thousand li apart in many towns.
units.literal: Sometimes within a single day people saw him in several places a thousand li away.

units.zh: 后失其符，为众鬼所杀。
units.en: He lost his charm and the ghosts tore him apart.
units.literal: Later he lost his talisman and was killed by the multitude of ghosts.

units.zh: 蓟子训
units.en: Ji Zixun
units.literal: Ji Zixun

units.zh: 蓟子训者，不知所由来也。
units.en: Ji Zixun's origins are unknown.
units.literal: As for Ji Zixun, no one knows whence he came.

units.zh: 建安中，客在济阴宛句。
units.en: During Jian'an he lodged at Wanyu in Jiyin.
units.literal: In the Jian'an era he was a guest in Wanyu in Jiyin.

units.zh: 有神异之道。
units.en: He worked wonders beyond nature.
units.literal: He had a way of divine strangeness.

units.zh: 尝抱邻家婴兒，故失手墯地而死，其父母惊号怨痛，不可忍闻，而子训唯谢以过误，终无它说，遂埋藏之。
units.en: He once held a neighbor's infant and purposely let it fall to the ground so that it died; the parents cried out in grief while he only apologized for a mistake, and then they buried it.
units.literal: He once embraced a neighbor's baby, purposely lost his grip so that it fell to the ground and died; its parents cried out in alarm and complained in grief, unbearable to hear, yet Zixun only apologized for a mistake, and in the end had nothing else to say, and therefore they buried it.

units.zh: 后月余，子训乃抱兒归焉。
units.en: A month later he walked in carrying the same child, alive.
units.literal: After more than a month Zixun then embraced the child and returned it.

units.zh: 父母大恐，曰：“死生异路，虽思我兒，乞不用复见也。”
units.en: They recoiled: "Dead and living do not mingle—we long for our son but beg you not to show him."
units.literal: The parents were greatly frightened and said, "Dead and living walk different roads; although we long for our child, we beg not to see him again."

units.zh: 兒识父母，轩渠笑悦，欲往就之，母不觉揽取，乃实兒也。
units.en: The boy knew them, crowed with joy, and leapt into his mother's arms—a living child.
units.literal: The child recognized its parents, laughed with delight, and wished to go to them; the mother unconsciously gathered it in her arms, and it was indeed the child.

units.zh: 虽大喜庆，心犹有疑。
units.en: Joy overwhelmed them, yet doubt lingered.
units.literal: Although there was great rejoicing, in their hearts they still had doubt.

units.zh: 乃窃发视死兒，但见衣被，方乃信焉。
units.en: They secretly opened the tiny grave and found only wrappings—then they believed.
units.literal: They therefore secretly opened and looked at the dead child, but saw only clothing and bedding, and only then believed.

units.zh: 于是子训流名京师，士大夫皆承风向慕之。
units.en: His fame rushed to Luoyang; every scholar-official yearned to meet him.
units.literal: Thereupon Zixun's name flowed to the capital; gentlemen and great officials all caught the wind and yearned toward him.

units.zh: 后乃驾驴车，与诸生俱诣许下。
units.en: He later hitched a donkey cart and rode to the capital with a train of pupils.
units.literal: Later he then drove a donkey cart and together with several students went to Xu below.

units.zh: 道过荥阳，止主人舍，而所驾之驴忽然卒僵，蛆虫流出，主遽白之。
units.en: At an Xingyang inn his donkey dropped dead, maggots pouring from its hide; the innkeeper panicked.
units.literal: Passing through Xingyang he stopped at his host's inn, and the donkey he was driving suddenly died stiff, maggots flowing out; the host hurriedly informed him.

units.zh: 子训曰：“乃尔乎？”
units.en: Zixun murmured, "So soon?"
units.literal: Zixun said, "Is it thus?"

units.zh: 方安坐饭，食毕，徐出以杖扣之，驴应声奋起，行步如初，即复进道。
units.en: He finished dinner in calm, tapped the carcass with his staff, and the beast sprang up sound as ever.
units.literal: He then sat calmly eating; when the meal was finished he slowly went out and tapped it with his staff; the donkey responded to the sound and leaped up, walking as at first, and immediately proceeded on the road again.

units.zh: 其追逐观者常有千数。
units.en: Crowds in the thousands chased his cart.
units.literal: Those who chased to watch were often a thousand or more in number.

units.zh: 既到京师，公卿以下候之者，坐上恒数百人，皆为设酒脯，终日不匮。
units.en: At Luoyang hundreds packed his hall; he fed them wine and meat all day without running dry.
units.literal: When he had reached the capital, from ministers of state downward those who waited for him—several hundred people constantly sat in his hall—he all set out wine and dried meat for them, and all day it was not exhausted.

units.zh: 后因遁去，遂不知所止。
units.en: Then he vanished, and none could trace him.
units.literal: Later because he slipped away, no one knew where he stopped.

units.zh: 初去之日，唯见白云腾起，从旦至暮，如是数十处。
units.en: The day he left, white pillars of cloud rose in dozens of places from dawn to dusk.
units.literal: On the day he first left, people only saw white clouds rise up, from dawn to dusk thus at several tens of places.

units.zh: 时有百岁翁，自说童兒时见子训卖药于会稽市，颜色不异于今。
units.en: A centenarian swore he had bought Zixun's physic in Kuaiji as a boy—the man's face had not aged.
units.literal: At that time there was a hundred-year-old man who himself said that in his childhood he had seen Zixun selling medicine in the market of Kuaiji, his complexion no different from now.

units.zh: 后人复于长安东霸城见之，与一老公共摩挲铜人，相谓曰：“适见铸此，已近五百岁矣。”
units.en: Later witnesses saw him east of Chang'an at Bawang, polishing a bronze statue with a greybeard, murmuring, "We watched them cast this—nearly five hundred years ago."
units.literal: Later people again saw him east of Chang'an at Bawang City, rubbing a bronze man together with an old man, saying to each other, "Just now we saw this cast; it is already nearly five hundred years."

units.zh: 顾视见人而去，犹驾昔所乘驴车也。
units.en: Spotting onlookers, they drove off in the same donkey cart as before.
units.literal: They looked around, saw people, and departed, still driving the same donkey cart they had formerly ridden.

units.zh: 见者呼之曰：“蓟先生小住。”
units.en: A bystander cried, "Wait, Master Ji!"
units.literal: Those who saw them called to them, saying, "Master Ji, pause a little."

units.zh: 并行应之，视若迟徐，而走马不及，于是而绝。
units.en: They answered while ambling, yet no horse could close the gap—and then they were gone.
units.literal: Walking in parallel they answered him; he looked as if he were slow, yet a galloping horse could not overtake him, and thus he was lost to sight.

units.zh: 刘根者，颍川人也。
units.en: Liu Gen hailed from Yingchuan.
units.literal: Liu Gen was a man of Yingchuan.

units.zh: 隐居嵩山中。
units.en: He hid himself on Mount Song.
units.literal: He concealed himself and lived in Mount Song.

units.zh: 诸好事者，自远而至，就根学道，太守史祈以根为妖妄，乃收执诣郡，数之曰：“汝有何术，而诬惑百姓？
units.en: Curious seekers trekked to study under him; Prefect Shi Qi branded him a charlatan, hauled him in, and demanded, "What trick lets you beguile the people?
units.literal: Various persons fond of such matters came from afar to study the Way with Gen; Grand Administrator Shi Qi thought Gen was deceitful and wild, and therefore arrested and seized him, brought him to the commandery, and reckoned with him, saying, "What arts do you have, that you delude and confuse the common people?

units.zh: 若果有神，可显一验事。
units.en: If spirits truly attend you, prove it once.
units.literal: If you truly have spirits, you can display one verification.

units.zh: 不尔，立死矣。”」
units.en: Otherwise you die on the spot."
units.literal: If not so, you will immediately die."

units.zh: 根曰：“实无它异，颇能令人见鬼耳。”
