units.en: Liu Gen said, "Nothing extraordinary; I can sometimes make people see ghosts."
units.literal: Liu Gen said, "In truth I have no other strangeness; I am only rather able to make people see ghosts."

units.zh: 祈曰：“促召之，使太守目睹，尔乃为明。”
units.en: Shi Qi barked, "Call them now—let this prefect see with his own eyes."
units.literal: Qi said, "Hasten to summon them; make the grand administrator witness with his own eyes, and only then is it clear."

units.zh: 根于是左顾而啸，有顷，祈之亡父祖近亲数十人，皆反缚在前，向根叩头曰：“小兒无状，分当万坐。”
units.en: Liu Gen glanced left and whistled; scores of Shi's dead kin appeared bound, kowtowed to Gen, and cried, "Our descendant is worthless—he deserves death a thousandfold."
units.literal: Gen therefore looked left and whistled; after a moment, several tens of Qi's deceased fathers, grandfathers, and close kin, all with arms bound behind, were in front, and toward Gen knocked their heads, saying, "The boy has no manners; by rights he deserves death ten thousand times."

units.zh: 顾而叱祈曰：“汝为子孙，不能有益先人，而反累辱亡灵！
units.en: They wheeled on Shi Qi: "You honor no ancestor yet heap shame on our shades!
units.literal: They looked back and berated Qi, saying, "You as descendant cannot benefit your forebears, yet instead repeatedly shame the spirits of the dead!

units.zh: 可叩头为吾陈谢。”」
units.en: Kowtow and beg his pardon on our behalf."
units.literal: You may kowtow and present my apology."

units.zh: 祈惊惧悲哀，顿首流血，请自甘罪坐。
units.en: Shi Qi blanched, beat his brow bloody, and begged to suffer in their stead.
units.literal: Qi was alarmed, afraid, and grieved; he knocked his head until blood flowed and begged to accept guilt and punishment himself.

units.zh: 根嘿而不应，忽然俱去，不知在所。
units.en: Liu Gen sat silent; the phantoms vanished without trace.
units.literal: Gen was silent and did not answer; suddenly they all departed, and no one knew where they were.

units.zh: 左慈字元放，庐江人也。
units.en: Zuo Ci, styled Yuanfang, came from Lujiang.
units.literal: Zuo Ci, courtesy name Yuanfang, was a man of Lujiang.

units.zh: 少有神道。
units.en: Even young he commanded uncanny arts.
units.literal: In his youth he had the way of spirits.

units.zh: 尝在司空曹操坐，操从容顾众宾曰：“今日高会，珍羞略备，所少吴松江鲈鱼耳。”
units.en: Once at a banquet hosted by Minister Cao Cao, Cao surveyed his guests and said, "We have every delicacy—only the perch of the Wu-Song is missing."
units.literal: He once sat in Minister of Works Cao Cao's company; Cao Cao leisurely looked around at the assembled guests and said, "Today's lofty gathering, rare delicacies are in general prepared; what is lacking is only the perch of the Wu-Song River."

units.zh: 放于下坐应曰：“此可得也。”
units.en: From the lower seats Zuo Ci answered, "That can be arranged."
units.literal: Ci from the lower seats replied, saying, "This can be obtained."

units.zh: 因求铜盘贮水，以竹竿饵钓于盘中，须臾引一鲈鱼出。
units.en: He asked for a copper pan of water, baited a bamboo rod in it, and in moments hauled up a Song perch.
units.literal: Therefore he sought a bronze basin to store water, baited a hook with a bamboo pole in the basin, and in a moment drew out one perch.

units.zh: 操大拊掌笑，会者皆惊。
units.en: Cao roared with laughter and slapped his thighs; every guest gaped.
units.literal: Cao Cao greatly clapped his hands and laughed; all who attended were astonished.

units.zh: 操曰：“一鱼不周坐席，可更得乎？”
units.en: Cao said, "One fish will not feed the table—can you fetch more?"
units.literal: Cao Cao said, "One fish does not suffice for the seats; can you get more?"

units.zh: 放乃更饵钩沉之，须臾复引出，皆长三尺余，生鲜可爱。
units.en: Zuo baited again, dipped the line, and pulled up more perch, each over three feet long, gleaming and firm.
units.literal: Fang then again baited his hook and sank it; in a moment he again drew them out; all were more than three chi in length, fresh and lovely to look at.

units.zh: 操使目前鱠之，周浃会者。
units.en: Cao had the fish sliced on the spot and passed the platters until every guest was served.
units.literal: Cao Cao had them sliced before his eyes for the assembly, so that it circulated to all who attended.

units.zh: 操又谓曰：“既已得鱼，恨无蜀中生姜耳。”
units.en: Cao added, "We have the fish, but no Sichuan ginger to season it."
units.literal: Cao Cao again said to him, "Since we have already obtained fish, I regret that we lack ginger from Shu."

units.zh: 放曰：“亦可得也。”」
units.en: Zuo said, "Ginger can be had as well."
units.literal: Fang said, "That too can be obtained."

units.zh: 操恐其近即所取，因曰：“吾前遣人到蜀买锦，可过敕使者，增市二端。”
units.en: Fearing he would conjure the root from thin air, Cao said, "I lately sent a man to Shu for brocade—tell that envoy to add two extra bolts to his order."
units.literal: Cao Cao feared he would fetch it from nearby on the spot, and therefore said, "Earlier I sent someone to Shu to buy brocade; you may pass by and instruct the envoy to add two bolts to the purchase."

units.zh: 语顷，即得姜还，并获操使报命。
units.en: A moment later he produced the ginger along with Cao's courier, clutching the receipt.
units.literal: In the space of speaking he obtained ginger and returned, and also captured Cao Cao's messenger reporting completion of the mission.

units.zh: 后操使蜀反，验问增锦之状及时日早晚，若符契焉。
units.en: When the real envoy returned from Shu, his report of the extra brocade matched Zuo's tale to the hour.
units.literal: Later when Cao Cao's envoy returned from Shu, he verified and asked about the circumstances of the added brocade and the early or late timing of the day; it was as if tally slips matched.

units.zh: 后操出近郊，士大夫从者百许人，慈乃为赍酒一升，脯一斤，手自斟酌，百官莫不醉饱。
units.en: Once Cao rode to the suburbs with a hundred officials; Zuo produced a pint of wine and a pound of jerky, poured for each man himself, and left every guest drunk and stuffed.
units.literal: Later Cao Cao went out to the near suburbs; more than a hundred gentlemen and great officials followed; Ci then for them brought one sheng of wine and one jin of dried meat, personally pouring for them, and none of the hundred officials failed to be drunk and full.

units.zh: 操怪之，使寻其故，行视诸垆，悉亡其酒脯矣。
units.en: Cao sent runners to trace the miracle—every tavern in town was missing the same wine and meat.
units.literal: Cao Cao thought it strange and sent men to seek the reason; going about to inspect the various wine-shops, all had lost their wine and dried meat.

units.zh: 操怀不喜，因坐上收，欲杀之，慈乃却入壁中，霍然不知所在。
units.en: Suspicious and angry, Cao ordered his arrest at table; Zuo stepped backward into the plaster and vanished.
units.literal: Cao Cao harbored displeasure, and therefore on the seat arrested him, intending to kill him; Ci then drew back into the wall, and in a flash no one knew where he was.

units.zh: 或见于市者，又捕之，而市人皆变形与慈同，莫知谁是。
units.en: Spotters cornered him in the market, yet every shopper wore Zuo's face—no one could tell which was real.
units.literal: When someone saw him in the market they again tried to seize him, but the people of the market all changed form to be identical with Ci, and no one knew which was he.

units.zh: 后人逢慈于阳城山头，因复逐之，遂入走羊群。
units.en: Later they sighted him on Yangcheng peak; chasing him, they watched him bolt into a flock of sheep.
units.literal: Later people encountered Ci on the summit of Yangcheng Mountain; they therefore again pursued him, and he thereupon entered and ran into a flock of sheep.

units.zh: 操知不可得，乃令就羊中告之曰：“不复相杀，本试君术耳。”
units.en: Cao saw capture was futile and shouted into the flock, "No more killing—I was only testing your skill."
units.literal: Cao Cao knew he could not be obtained, and therefore ordered someone to go among the sheep and announce to them, saying, "I will not kill you again; originally I was only testing your arts."

units.zh: 忽有一老羝屈前两膝，人立而言曰：“遽如许。”
units.en: An old ram rose on its knees like a man and bleated, "Why such haste?"
units.literal: One old ram knelt like a person, saying, "Why are you hurrying so?"

units.zh: 即竞往赴之，而群羊数百皆变为羝，并屈前膝人立，云“遽如许”，遂莫知所取焉。
units.en: The hunters rushed the speaker—only to see hundreds of rams kneel upright, each crying the same phrase, so none could pick the sage.
units.literal: They immediately all rushed to go to it, but several hundred sheep in the flock all changed into rams, all bending their foreknees and standing like humans, saying "So suddenly like this," and therefore none knew which to take.

units.zh: 计子勋
units.en: Ji Zixūn
units.literal: Ji Zixūn

units.zh: 计子勋者，不知何郡县人，皆谓数百步，行来于人间。
units.en: Ji Zixūn's home county is lost; folk said he paced a few hundred steps at a time as he wandered among them.
units.literal: As for Ji Zixun, no one knew from what commandery or county he was; all said that for several hundred paces he walked back and forth among mankind.

units.zh: 一旦忽言日中当死，主人与之葛衣，子勋服而正寝，至日中果死。
units.en: One dawn he announced he would die at noon; his host gave him a hemp robe, he lay down composed—and at noon he was dead.
units.literal: One morning he suddenly said that at midday he ought to die; his host gave him a kudzu garment, Zixun put it on and lay straight as for sleep, and when midday came he indeed died.

units.zh: 上成公者，密县人也。
units.en: The adept Shang Chenggong came from Mi county.
units.literal: Shang Chenggong was a man of Mi county.

units.zh: 其初行久而不還，後歸，語其家云：「我已得仙。」
units.en: He once vanished for ages, then returned to tell his kin, "I have become an immortal."
units.literal: At first he walked a long time and did not return; later he returned and said to his family, "I have already obtained immortality."

units.zh: 因辞家而去。
units.en: He bade them farewell and left.
units.literal: Thereupon he took leave of his family and departed.

units.zh: 家人见其举步稍高，良久乃没云。
units.en: They watched each stride lift him higher until he faded into the clouds.
units.literal: The family members saw that each step he took was somewhat higher, and after a long while he then disappeared into the clouds.

units.zh: 陈寔、韩韶同见其事。
units.en: Chen Shi and Han Shao both saw it happen.
units.literal: Chen Shi and Han Shao together witnessed this affair.

units.zh: 解奴辜、张貂
units.en: Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao
units.literal: Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao

units.zh: 解奴辜、张貂者，亦不知是何郡国人也。
units.en: Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao likewise left no record of their native place.
units.literal: As for Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao, likewise no one knew from what commandery or kingdom they were.

units.zh: 皆能隐沦，出入不由门户。
units.en: Both could melt from view and pass through walls without doors.
units.literal: Both were able to conceal themselves and sink from sight, going in and out without using doors or gates.

units.zh: 奴辜能变易物形，以诳幻人。
units.en: Nugu could reshape objects to bewilder the eye.
units.literal: Nugu was able to change the forms of things in order to delude and dazzle people.

units.zh: 又河南有□圣卿，善为丹书符劾，厌杀鬼神而使命之。
units.en: Henan also had a certain Shengqing—one character of his name is lost in the text—who painted cinnabar talismans, smothered malignant spirits, and drafted them as servants.
units.literal: Also in Henan there was □ Shengqing, skilled at making cinnabar writings and talismanic binding, suppressing and killing ghosts and spirits and commanding them to run errands.

units.zh: 又有编盲意，亦与鬼物交通。
units.en: Another wonder-worker, Bian Mangyi, trafficked with ghosts as well.
units.literal: There was also Bian Mangyi, who likewise had intercourse with ghostly things.

units.zh: 初，章帝时有寿光侯者，能劾百鬼众魅，令自缚见形。
units.en: In Emperor Zhang's reign Marquis Shouguang could arraign legions of sprites and force each to show its true body.
units.literal: In the beginning, under Emperor Zhang there was a man Marquis Shouguang who was able to impeach the hundred ghosts and the multitude of goblins, making them bind themselves and show their forms.

units.zh: 其乡人有妇为魅所病，侯为劾之，得大蛇数丈，死于门外。
units.en: When a neighbor's wife fell under a demon, he bound the creature and produced a dead serpent many yards long outside her gate.
units.literal: A fellow villager had a woman afflicted by a goblin; the marquis impeached it for her and obtained a great snake several zhang long, dead outside the gate.

units.zh: 又有神树，人止者辄死，鸟过者必坠，侯复劾之，树盛夏枯落，见大蛇长七八丈，悬死其间。
units.en: A spirit tree killed every traveler and dropped every bird that flew past; he exorcised it in midsummer until it shed its leaves, revealing a seven- or eight-yard serpent strangled in the crown.
units.literal: There was also a divine tree: anyone who stopped there always died, and any bird that passed was sure to fall; the marquis again impeached it; in the height of summer the tree withered and dropped its leaves, and they saw a great snake seven or eight zhang long hanging dead within it.

units.zh: 帝闻而征之。
units.en: The court summoned him on report of these feats.
units.literal: The emperor heard of him and summoned him.

units.zh: 乃试问之：“吾殿下夜半后，常有数人，绛衣被发，持火相随，岂能劾之乎？”
units.en: The emperor tested him: "After midnight beneath my hall crimson phantoms with loose hair parade with torches—can you bind them?"
units.literal: He then tried asking him, "Below my hall, after midnight, there are always several persons in crimson robes with loosened hair, carrying torches and following one another—can you impeach them?"

units.zh: 侯曰：“此小怪，易销耳。”
units.en: Shouguang said, "Petty sprites—easily dismissed."
units.literal: The marquis said, "These are small goblins; easy to dispose of."

units.zh: 帝伪使三人为之，侯劾三人，登时仆地无气。
units.en: The emperor sent three living attendants to fake the apparition; Shouguang's spell flattened all three, breathless.
units.literal: The emperor falsely had three men do it; the marquis impeached the three men, and immediately they collapsed to the ground without breath.

units.zh: 帝大惊曰：“非魅也，朕相试耳。”
units.en: The emperor cried, "Those were living men. I was only testing you."
units.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed and said, "These are not goblins; I was testing you."

units.zh: 解之而苏。
units.en: He lifted the curse and they stirred awake.
units.literal: He released them and they revived.

units.zh: 甘始、东郭延年、封君达三人者，皆方士也。
units.en: Gan Shi, Dongguo Yannian, and Feng Junda were wandering adepts.
units.literal: Gan Shi, Dongguo Yannian, and Feng Junda—these three men were all recipe gentlemen.

units.zh: 率能行容成御妇人术，或饮小便，或自倒悬，爱啬精气，不极视大言。
units.en: They practiced Rongcheng's sexual yoga, drank their own urine, hung head-down, hoarded vital breath, and shunned strain and shouting.
units.literal: Generally they were able to practice Lord Rongcheng's method of controlling women in intercourse, or drink urine, or hang themselves upside down; they cherished and hoarded essential qi and did not exhaust themselves with staring or loud speech.

units.zh: 甘始、元放、延年皆为操所录，问其术而行之。
units.en: Cao Cao retained Gan Shi, Zuo Ci, and Yannian, questioned their regimens, and tried them himself.
units.literal: Gan Shi, Zuo Ci styled Yuanfang, and Yannian were all taken into service by Cao Cao, who asked about their arts and practiced them.

units.zh: 君达号“青牛师”。
units.en: Feng Junda was known as the Black Ox Master.
units.literal: Junda was styled "Master of the Black Ox."

units.zh: 凡此数人，皆百余岁及二百岁也。
units.en: Each of them passed a century, some two hundred years.
units.literal: All these several persons lived beyond a hundred years and up to two hundred years.

units.zh: 王真、郝孟节
units.en: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie
units.literal: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie

units.zh: 王真、郝孟节者，皆上党人也。
units.en: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie came from Shangdang.
units.literal: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie were both men of Shangdang.

units.zh: 王真年且百岁，视之面有光泽，似未五十者。
units.en: Wang Zhen neared a hundred yet glowed like a man under fifty.
units.literal: Wang Zhen's years were nearly a hundred; looking at him, his face had luster, as though he were not yet fifty.

units.zh: 自云：“周流登五岳名山，悉能行胎息胎食之方，嗽舌下泉咽之，不绝房室。”
units.en: He claimed, "I have climbed the five sacred peaks, can swallow embryonic breath and embryonic essences, press the saliva under my tongue and drink it down, and never renounce sexual life."
units.literal: He himself said, "I have roamed and ascended the five marchmounts and famous mountains, and in all cases am able to practice the methods of embryonic breathing and embryonic eating; I rinse the spring beneath the tongue and swallow it; I do not cut off intercourse with the bedchamber."

units.zh: 孟节能含枣核，不食可至五年十年。
units.en: Hao Mengjie could hold a date stone under his tongue and fast five or ten years.
units.literal: Mengjie was able to hold a jujube pit in his mouth and not eat yet reach five or ten years.

units.zh: 又能结气不息，身不动摇，状若死人，可至百日半年。
units.en: He could seal his breath, lie motionless as a corpse, for half a year at a stretch.
units.literal: He was also able to knot his qi without ceasing, his body not swaying, appearing like a dead man, for up to a hundred days or half a year.

units.zh: 亦有室家。
units.en: He still kept a household.
units.literal: He also had wife and family.

units.zh: 为人质谨不妄言，似士君子。
units.en: Plain-spoken and cautious, he bore himself like a scholar.
units.literal: In personality he was plain and careful and did not speak rashly; he seemed a gentleman among scholars.

units.zh: 曹操使领诸方士焉。
units.en: Cao Cao put him in charge of the court's roster of adepts.
units.literal: Cao Cao had him oversee the various recipe gentlemen.

units.zh: 刘和平
units.en: Wang Heping
units.literal: Wang Heping

units.zh: 北海王和平，性好道术，自以当仙。
units.en: Wang Heping of Beihai loved Daoist arts and was sure he would transcend.
units.literal: Wang Heping of Beihai by nature loved the arts of the Way and believed himself destined to become an immortal.

units.zh: 济南孙邕少事之，从至京师。
units.en: Sun Yong of Jinan studied under him in youth and followed him to Luoyang.
units.literal: Sun Yong of Jinan in his youth served him and followed him to the capital.

units.zh: 会和平病殁，邕因葬之东陶。
units.en: When Wang died of illness, Sun buried him at East Tao.
units.literal: It happened that Heping died of illness; Yong therefore buried him at East Tao.

units.zh: 有书百余卷，药数囊，悉以送之。
units.en: Over a hundred fascicles of scripture and several sacks of elixirs went into the tomb with the corpse.
units.literal: There were more than a hundred scrolls of writings and several bags of drugs, all of which were sent down into the grave with him.

units.zh: 后弟子夏荣言其尸解，邕乃恨不取其宝书仙药焉。
units.en: Later the disciple Xia Rong claimed Wang had undergone corpse release; Sun Yong rued the lost scriptures and elixirs he had left underground.
units.literal: Later his disciple Xia Rong said that he had undergone corpse liberation; Yong therefore regretted not having taken his precious books and immortal drugs.

units.zh: 赞曰：幽贶罕征，明数难校。
units.en: Verdict: Heaven's covert signs rarely show themselves; reason cannot easily test them.
units.literal: The encomium states: Heaven's hidden boons are seldom proven manifest; luminous reckoning is hard to verify.

units.zh: 不探精远，歇感灵效？
units.en: Without plumbing the farthest depths, who can fathom such powers?
units.literal: If one does not investigate the recondite and remote, how can one exhaustively perceive spiritual efficacy?

units.zh: 如或迁讹，实乖玄奥。
units.en: Distorted tales only betray the mystery they claim to praise.
units.literal: If perchance there is shifting error, it truly contradicts the arcane subtlety.

units.zh: 請前越巂太守荀翌為從事中郎，辟潁川陳寔為屬：共定計策。
units.en: he named the former governor of Yuegui, Xun Yi, as staff supervisor and recruited Chen Shi of Yingchuan as an aide, and with them he hammered out a strategy.
units.literal: requested the former governor of Yuegui Xun Yi as staff supervisor, summoned Chen Shi of Yingchuan as subordinate: together they settled plans and strategy.

units.zh: 太祖渡江，以秦從龍薦，發書聘之，引伊、呂、諸葛為喻。
units.en: After the Founder crossed the Yangzi, Qin Conglong recommended him; the Founder sent a letter of invitation comparing Chen to Yi Yin, Lü Shang, and Zhuge Liang.
units.literal: When the Founder crossed the river, on Qin Conglong's recommendation he sent a letter to engage him, citing Yi, Lü, and Zhuge as analogies.

units.zh: 贼张步拥兵据齐，上遣伏隆谕步，许降。
units.en: The warlord Zhang Bu held Qi with an army; the emperor sent Fu Long to negotiate and accepted his offer to submit.
units.literal: The bandit Zhang Bu held troops and occupied Qi; the sovereign sent Fu Long to instruct Bu, promising acceptance of surrender.

units.zh: 旋复叛称王，至五年中乃破。
units.en: He soon rebelled again, proclaimed himself king, and was not crushed until mid–Jianwu 5.
units.literal: Soon he again rebelled and declared himself king; down to the middle of the fifth year he was then broken.

units.zh: 淮陽王舅張博、魏郡太守京房坐窺道諸侯王以邪意，漏泄省中語，博要斬，房棄市。
units.en: Zhang Bo, maternal uncle of the King of Huaiyang, and Jing Fang, governor of Wei commandery, were convicted of spying on the feudal kings with evil intent and leaking palace secrets. Bo was condemned to beheading, and Fang was executed in the marketplace.
units.literal: Huaiyang King maternal uncle Zhang Bo, Wei commandery governor Jing Fang convicted spied on feudal lords kings with evil intent, leaked revealed palace secret words, Bo condemned beheaded, Fang executed in marketplace.

units.zh: 武召侍御史河閒劉儵，參問其國中王子侯之賢者，儵稱解瀆亭侯宏。
units.en: Dou Wu called in the attendant censor Liu Shu of Hejian and asked which of the imperial clansmen there was fit to rule; Liu Shu recommended Liu Hong, Marquis of the Jiedu pavilion.
units.literal: Wu summoned attendant censor Liu Shu of Hejian, consulted him on worthy princes and marquises in that state, and Shu praised Marquis Hong of the Jiedu pavilion.

units.zh: 武入白太后，遂徵立之，是為靈帝。
units.en: Dou Wu laid the matter before the empress dowager; Liu Hong was summoned and enthroned as Emperor Ling.
units.literal: Wu entered and reported to the empress dowager; then (Hong) was summoned and established; this was Emperor Ling.

units.zh: 帝既立，論定策功，更封武為聞喜侯；
units.en: Once the new emperor was enthroned, those who had settled the succession were rewarded, and Dou Wu received a further enfeoffment as Marquis of Wenxi;
units.literal: When the emperor had been established, they assessed merit in settling the succession, and Wu was further enfeoffed marquis of Wenxi;

units.zh: 〈孙盛曰：夫玄览未然，逆鉴来事，虽裨灶、梓慎其犹病诸，况术之下此者乎？
units.en: 〈Sun Sheng notes even canonical astrologers stumbled—lesser tricks merit doubt.
units.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: To survey the unseen and mirror coming events—even Pi Zao and Zi Shen struggled—how much more arts beneath theirs?

units.zh: 而以裨、梓限之，谓达为妄，非笃论也。
units.en: Equating him with Pi Zao sells Zhao Da short.
units.literal: Yet limiting him with Pi and Zi—calling Da deluded—is not serious judgment.

units.zh: 孝章皇帝深惟古人之道，助三正之微，定律著令，冀承天心，順物性命，以致時雍。
units.en: Emperor Zhang pondered antiquity, harmonized the three beginnings in law, and hoped to align Heaven with the nature of things for universal peace.
units.literal: Emperor Zhang deeply pondered the Way of ancients, assisting the subtlety of the three beginnings; fixing statutes and establishing orders; hoping to inherit Heaven's heart, comply with creatures' natures and lives, so as to bring seasonal harmony.

units.zh: 肅宗集諸儒於白虎觀，恭特以經明得召，與其議。
units.en: When Emperor Zhang convened scholars at White Tiger Hall, Gong was invited on strength of his classical expertise and joined the debates.
units.literal: Emperor Suzong assembled the Confucians at White Tiger Hall; Gong was specially summoned because of his clarity on the classics and participated in their discussions.

units.zh: 初，肅宗時，斷獄皆以冬至之前，自後論者互多駁異。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhang capital cases had to conclude before the winter solstice; later scholars quarreled endlessly over the rule.
units.literal: Formerly, in Emperor Suzong's time, cutting prison cases was all before the winter solstice; afterward debaters mutually increased refutations and differences.

units.zh: 建初元年，肅宗詔舉賢良方正，大司農劉寬舉丕。
units.en: In Jianchu 1 Emperor Zhang sought worthy candidates; Minister of Agriculture Liu Kuan nominated Lu Pi.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianchu, Emperor Suzong ordered recommendation of worthy and upright men; Minister of Agriculture Liu Kuan recommended Pi.

units.zh: 其後帝巡狩之趙，特被引見，難問經傳，厚加賞賜。
units.en: Later, when the emperor toured Zhao, Pi was specially summoned, examined on the classics, and richly rewarded.
units.literal: Afterward, when the emperor toured Zhao, Pi was specially summoned for audience, questioned on the classics, and richly rewarded.

units.zh: 議未即行，侍中廣漢董扶私謂焉曰：「京師將亂，益州分野有天子氣。」
units.en: Before the plan could take effect, Palace Attendant Dong Fu of Guanghan took him aside: “Luoyang is heading for turmoil, and the stars over Yizhou show the aura of an emperor.”
units.literal: The proposal had not yet been put into effect when Palace Attendant Dong Fu of Guanghan privately said to Yan: “The capital is about to be in chaos; in the astrological field of Yizhou there is the qi of the Son of Heaven.”

units.zh: 陳壽《益部耆舊傳》曰：董扶字茂安。
units.en: Chen Shou’s Records of Elders of Yibu records: Dong Fu, courtesy name Mao’an.
units.literal: Chen Shou’s Records of Elders of Yibu says: Dong Fu, courtesy name Mao’an.

units.zh: 至止，言人莫能當，所至而談止也。
units.en: “Zhizhi”—“the one who stops all talk”—for wherever he went debate fell silent.
units.literal: [Zhizhi “to the stop”], meaning no one could withstand him—wherever he went discussion ceased.

units.zh: 焉聞扶言，意更在益州。
units.en: Those words fixed his mind on Yizhou more firmly than ever.
units.literal: When Yan heard Fu’s words, his intentions turned still more toward Yizhou.

units.zh: 在朝稱為儒宗，甚見器重。
units.en: At court he was hailed as the leading Confucian scholar and won deep respect.
units.literal: At court he was called the patriarch of scholars and was greatly valued and trusted.

units.zh: 於是靈帝徵扶，即拜侍中。
units.en: Emperor Ling then summoned Dong Fu and appointed him palace attendant on the spot.
units.literal: Thereupon Emperor Ling summoned Fu and immediately appointed him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 遂至京師，遊覽太學，還家講授，弟子自遠而至。
units.en: He went to the capital, studied at the Imperial Academy, then returned home to teach; students came from far and wide.
units.literal: Then he reached the capital, toured the Imperial Academy, returned home to lecture and teach, and disciples came from afar.

units.zh: 永康元年167年，日有蝕之，詔舉賢良方正之士，策問得失。
units.en: In 167, the first year of Yongkang, a solar eclipse prompted an edict summoning worthy and upright candidates for written policy examinations.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, 167, there was a solar eclipse; an edict summoned worthy and upright candidates, and policy questions were put on gains and losses.

units.zh: 左馮翊趙謙等舉扶，扶以病不詣，遙於長安上封事，遂稱疾篤歸家。
units.en: Zhao Qian of Zuofengyi and others recommended him, but Fu pleaded illness and stayed away, submitting a sealed memorial from Chang’an before declaring himself gravely ill and going home.
units.literal: Zuo Fengyi Zhao Qian and others recommended Fu; Fu, citing illness, did not go; from afar at Chang’an he submitted a sealed memorial, then claimed grave illness and returned home.

units.zh: 扶出一歲而靈帝崩，天下大亂。
units.en: A year after he left the capital Emperor Ling died and the empire plunged into chaos.
units.literal: Fu had been out one year when Emperor Ling died and the realm fell into great chaos.

units.zh: 巴西趙韙去官，俱隨焉。
units.en: Zhao Wei of Baxi, director of the Imperial Granary, resigned his post, and both men went with Liu Yan.
units.literal: Zhao Wei of Baxi, director of the Imperial Granary, left office, and both followed Yan.

units.zh: 後去官，年八十二卒於家。
units.en: He later resigned and died at home at eighty-two.
units.literal: Later he left office; at age eighty-two he died at home.

units.zh: 扶亦求為蜀郡西部屬國都尉，及太倉令
units.en: Dong Fu likewise sought appointment as commandant of the dependent state in western Shu Commandery.
units.literal: Dong Fu also requested appointment as commandant of the dependent state in the western part of Shu Commandery.

units.zh: 大將軍何進表薦扶曰：「資遊、夏之德，述孔氏之風，內懷焦、董消復之術。
units.en: Grand General He Jin memorialized in his favor: “He has the virtue of the ancient sages You and Xia, carries forward Confucius’s teaching, and holds within him the restorative arts of Jiao and Dong.
units.literal: Grand General He Jin memorialized recommending Fu, saying: “He possesses the virtue of You and Xia, expounds the style of the Kong clan, and inwardly holds the restorative arts of Jiao and Dong.

units.zh: 始扶發辭抗論，益部少雙，故號曰
units.en: From the start his debating was unmatched in Yizhou, so he was nicknamed
units.literal: At first, when Fu began to speak in refutation and debate, few in Yibu could match him; therefore he was styled

units.zh: （致止）
units.en: Some manuscripts read “Zhizhi” (“he who stops”).
units.literal: (zhizhi “to stop” [variant])

units.zh: 後丞相諸葛亮問秦宓以扶所長，宓曰：「董扶褒秋毫之善，貶纖芥之惡。」
units.en: Later Chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi what Dong Fu excelled at. Mi replied: “Dong Fu praises goodness down to the finest hair and condemns wrongdoing down to the smallest flaw.”
units.literal: Later Chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi about Fu’s strengths; Mi said: “Dong Fu praises the good even in an autumn down, and condemns evil even in a fiber of grass.”

units.zh: 子福。
units.en: His son was named Fu.
units.literal: Son Fu.

units.zh: 詣涪，
units.en: He went on to Fu,
units.literal: went to Fu,

units.zh: 靈帝末，黨禁解，大將軍何進聞而辟之。
units.en: Near the end of Lingdi's reign the ban ended; He Jin the general-in-chief heard of him and called him in.
units.literal: At the end of the Ling Emperor's reign the partisan prohibition was lifted; the general-in-chief He Jin heard of him and summoned him.

units.zh: 州郡以進權威，不敢違意，遂迫脅玄，不得已而詣之。
units.en: Local authorities, awed by He Jin, pressed Zheng Xuan until he had no choice but to present himself.
units.literal: The commanderies and prefectures, because of Jin's awesome power, did not dare disobey his intent, and therefore coerced Xuan; unable to avoid it, he went to him.

units.zh: 進為設几杖，禮待甚優。
units.en: He Jin set out a couch and cane and treated him with exceptional respect.
units.literal: Jin for him set out a bench and staff and treated him with the utmost courtesy.

units.zh: 同志者乃共刻石立碑，蔡邕爲其文，旣而謂涿郡盧植曰：「吾爲碑銘多矣，皆有慙德，唯郭有道無愧色耳。」
units.en: His admirers raised a stone stele with an inscription by Cai Yong, who later told Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: "I have composed countless epitaphs, and most leave me uneasy about my own character—only Guo Youdao's leaves me untroubled."
units.literal: Those of like mind then together carved stone and erected a stele; Cai Yong composed its text. Afterwards he said to Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: "I have written many stele inscriptions, and in all I have felt shame for my virtue—only for Guo Youdao do I feel no shame."

units.zh: 明年春，卒于家，時年四十二。
units.en: The following spring he died at home at the age of forty-two.
units.literal: The next spring he died at home, aged forty-two.

units.zh: 昔蕭何之鎮關中，荀彧之居許下，不亦異於是乎！
units.en: Long ago Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu held Xudu — were they not utterly unlike this?
units.literal: In old days when Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu dwelt at Xudu — were they not utterly unlike this?

units.zh: 元康曰：「嘗讀《崔琰傳》，追恨魏武不弘。
units.en: Yuankang said, "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.
units.literal: Yuankang said: "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.
